item.description: arXiv:2610.18698v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct an approximate sampler for finite doubly free-boundary Macdonald rail-yard processes with Macdonald, boundary, and edge parameters in $(0,1)$. The construction allows arbitrary finite sequences of additions and removals of horizontal or vertical strips and all four boundary types. It reverses a finite commutation--reflection history from a partition sequence whose entries are equal, with the common partition weighted by both boundaries. We derive local reconstruction kernels from the skew Cauchy, Littlewood, and branching identities. Bulk and boundary updates combine integer increments with conditional shape sampling at a prescribed size; same-sign swaps use finite conditional resampling. For $K$ reflection periods and an initial partition-size cutoff $M$, the algorithm terminates almost surely and samples the resulting approximating law exactly. We prove total variation convergence to the target process as $K,M\to\infty$ and give explicit bounds for both truncation errors, decaying geometrically in the cutoffs for fixed input parameters. Under fixed parameter bounds, we also bound the expected operation count of direct enumeration in a unit-cost model. We further construct an exact rejection sampler for the initial partition law without a size cutoff or evaluation of its normalizing constant. Using this sampler removes the size-truncation error, leaving only the error from the finite reflection history.
item.dc:creator: Zhongyang Li

item.title: A formula for the free energy of non-convex vector spin glasses
item.description: arXiv:2610.18744v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider vector mean-field spin glass models with independent and identically distributed spins without assuming the covariance function is convex. We identify the limit free energy as the minimum of a functional that can be written as the sum of a relative entropy and the solution of a Hamilton--Jacobi equation. The proof of this result relies on the observation that when the spin configurations of the system are constrained to have a given empirical measure, the corresponding free energy approximately satisfies a Hamilton--Jacobi equation with a uniformly bounded error.
item.dc:creator: Hong-Bin Chen, Fu-Hsuan Ho, Victor Issa

item.title: Branching explosion of Brownian Fleming-Viot systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.18802v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We resolve the long-standing non-extinction problem for Brownian Fleming-Viot systems in bounded domains. For every fixed N >= 3, we construct a bounded connected domain in R3 in which branching explosion occurs with positive probability before every prescribed positive time, from every interior initial configuration. On this event all particles converge to one boundary point. Together with two-particle non-extinction, this gives the sharp population threshold for bounded-domain Brownian explosion. The mechanism is directed transport generated by uniform copying in a periodic absorbing environment. We compute a positive cubic current for the same two-harmonic killing profile at every N >= 3, with an explicit population coefficient and a controlled fourth-order remainder. To realize this transport by spherical absorption, we develop a marked genealogical transfer theorem that retains the Euclidean displacement inherited at each copy. Common ancestry makes the integer winding reconstructible from phase records and yields convergence of the stationary signed current. A boundary restart law with P'olya weights supplies the continuity needed to turn that current into stable escape. Diffusion coefficients adapted to a common Kelvin clock preserve the joint Brownian law and uniform donor marks while compressing escape into finite lifetime. Disjoint spherical holes in a ball accumulate only at the explosion point. The boundary is smooth elsewhere, with finite area and perimeter. Boundary area within distance r of the singularity is of order r. For three particles, the transfer theorem covers every smooth positive periodic killing rate.
item.dc:creator: Yaohui Lin, Tiankui Lu

item.title: Superdiffusive Invariance Principle for the two-dimensional Asymmetric Simple Exclusion Process
item.description: arXiv:2610.18847v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the Asymmetric Simple Exclusion Process (ASEP) at its critical dimension $d=2$, started from the Bernoulli product measure with density $\rho \in (0,1)$. We first derive the sharp $\log(t)^{2/3}$ divergence of the bulk diffusivity, predicted via mode-coupling theory in [H. van Beijeren, R. Kutner, H. Spohn, Phys. Rev. Lett., 1985], including the exact prefactor, thereby removing the subleading diverging multiplicative corrections in the Tauberian bounds of [H.-T. Yau, Ann. of Math., 2004]. More importantly, we establish an invariance principle for the density fluctuation field on the corresponding superdiffusive scales. On the time scale $\tau$, we rescale space by $\sqrt{\tau} \log(\tau)^{1/3}$ in the direction of the drift and by $\sqrt{\tau}$ in the transverse direction, and prove functional convergence of the rescaled fluctuation process to the solution of a conservative stochastic heat equation with additive noise. This is the same explicit Gaussian Fixed Point obtained in [G. Cannizzaro, Q. Moulard, F. Toninelli, arXiv:2501.00344, 2025] for the two-dimensional Stochastic Burgers Equation (SBE). We also deduce a superdiffusive central limit theorem for the second-class particle under the same anisotropic rescaling. The result holds for any finite-range jump kernel with nonzero drift and uniaxial asymmetry. This is the first space-time scaling limit result for a nonequilibrium interacting particle system at the critical dimension, where Gaussian fluctuations emerge despite logarithmic corrections to the scaling. The proof uses an approximate fluctuation-dissipation relation, which is obtained by combining a sharp quantitative comparison between the ASEP and SBE generators with refined estimates on the SBE Ansatz. An additional key novelty is a tightness argument that overcomes the limitations of the It\^o trick on superdiffusive scales.
item.dc:creator: Quentin Moulard

item.title: A Stochastic Analysis Perspective on Diffusion Models
item.description: arXiv:2610.14133v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Generative modelling involves two complementary tasks: learning a probabilistic approximation of an unknown data distribution from observations, and designing a tractable mechanism for sampling from this approximation. We present a stochastic-analysis perspective on score-based generative models, connecting ideas from classical sampling theory, score estimation, and diffusion time reversal. We first explain how score functions link Langevin sampling with score matching, and how Gaussian smoothing leads to denoising score matching and multiscale sampling methods. We then emphasize the distinction between dynamics preserving a fixed distribution and dynamics transporting a prescribed family of marginals. This motivates a path-space treatment of diffusion time reversal. Finally, we connect the ideal reverse diffusion with practical generative algorithms.
item.dc:creator: Stanislas Strasman (SU, LPSM)

item.title: Optimal strong convergence of a splitting mixed finite element method for a stochastic Keller--Segel system
item.description: arXiv:2610.14390v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this work, we develop and analyze a splitting mixed finite element method, combined with a fully implicit Euler time discretization, for a stochastic Keller--Segel system with general polynomial logistic growth and multiplicative noise. The proposed splitting formulation allows the use of standard finite element spaces without requiring the LBB inf--sup condition associated with traditional mixed finite element methods and, at each time step, avoids the need for solving a coupled nonlinear system. We first establish the well-posedness of the variational solution and derive new high-moment, higher-order regularity, and exponential stability estimates. These estimates provide the key analytical foundation for the strong convergence analysis of the numerical method. A principal contribution of this work is the derivation of error estimates directly in full expectation, without the use of localization arguments. By combining the new stability and regularity estimates with a stochastic Gronwall framework, we overcome the difficulties arising from the interaction between the nonlinear chemotactic coupling and the multiplicative noise. As a result, we establish strong convergence in high-moment norms and obtain optimal convergence rates with respect to both the temporal and spatial discretizations. In particular, the proposed method achieves the optimal rates of order $k^{\frac{1}{2}}$ in time and $h$ in space in the relevant $L^2$- and $H^1$-based error norms. These results provide, to our knowledge, the first optimal strong convergence analysis in full expectation for a splitting mixed finite element approximation of this class of stochastic Keller--Segel systems.
item.dc:creator: Liet Vo

item.title: Harmonic Reduction of Spin-Coupled Grover Walks on Hypercubes via Quantum Bernoulli Noises
item.description: arXiv:2610.14467v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We consider spin-coupled Grover walks on hypercubes within the framework of quantum Bernoulli noises (QBN). We identify parity-dependent harmonic subspaces generated by the central Hamming layers: in even dimension they give a fixed-point subspace, whereas in odd dimension the walk reduces on the harmonic subspace to an explicit eight-dimensional reduced dynamics. Using symmetric-group representation theory, we characterize the corresponding isotypic structure and determine the reduced spectrum. The harmonic reduction also yields explicit long-time probability behavior and shows that the resulting states may occupy an asymptotically vanishing fraction of the hypercube while still spanning its full Hamming diameter.
item.dc:creator: Ce Wang

item.title: Duality Theory for Filter Stability in Hidden Markov Models
item.description: arXiv:2610.15085v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This article is concerned with the problem of nonlinear (stochastic) filter stability for a discrete time hidden Markov model (HMM) with finite state and observation spaces. For this purpose, a comprehensive duality theory is developed whereby the dual control system is a backward stochastic difference equation (BSDE). The duality is expressed in two inter-related forms. In its variational form, the minimum mean squared error of optimal filtering equals the value of a dual optimal control problem. In its structural form, controllability (resp. stabilizability) of the BSDE and observability (resp. detectability) of the HMM are dual properties. The dual optimal control problem supplies the Lyapunov function and the dissipation: the former is the value function (a variance), the latter the optimal running cost accumulated over the horizon. The main result is an invariance principle: under any one of three model properties---ergodicity of the Markov matrix, or observability or detectability of the HMM---zero dissipation over a finite horizon forces the Lyapunov function to vanish. A converse is also obtained: detectability is necessary. Two applications are given. The first is filter stability in chi-squared divergence: the invariance principle is applied in the manner of LaSalle, to limits of trajectories along which the dissipation vanishes asymptotically, the role of the model properties being to render the zero-dissipation set trivial. The second is a quantitative form of the invariance principle, through a Poincare constant, from which convergence rates follow. Both the model properties that govern stability and the Lyapunov function that certifies it are thus obtained from a dual optimal control problem, as in the classical theory for the linear Gaussian model.
item.dc:creator: Prashant G. Mehta

item.title: Closed forms all the way up: the sample variance of four observations
item.description: arXiv:2610.15174v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The distribution function $F(y)=\Pr(S^2\le y)$ of the sample variance $S^2$ of four independent observations is elementary on its entire support for every polynomial parent density on $[0,1]$ (without loss of generality), and we give it in finite closed form for the uniform, Beta$(2,1)$ and Beta$(2,2)$ parents. The support splits at $y = 1/6$, $2/9$ and $1/4$, with the ceiling at $1/3$, all fixed by geometry: in coordinates aligned with the cube diagonal the event $S^2\le y$ is a ball of radius $\sqrt{3y}$, the cube projects to a rhombic dodecahedron, and these are the levels at which the ball reaches its faces, edges and two kinds of vertices. The divergence theorem reduces every moment of the clipped ball to integrals along circular arcs, so each regime closes in algebraic functions of $\sqrt{y}$ and inverse trigonometric functions. For the uniform parent the only non-obvious constant is $K_g = 12\sqrt2\arctan\sqrt2$, proportional to the mean width of the cuboctahedron; the Beta constants are rational expressions in $\pi$, $\sqrt2$, $\sqrt3$ and $\arctan\sqrt2$, as in the uniform case. At $n = 4$ the normal-theory $\chi^2$ recipe used in acceptance testing misplaces the $99$th percentile of $S^2$ by $50\%$ for the uniform parent. For three observations, polynomial parents also give elementary closed forms (arXiv:2609.25333), but two elementary cases in a row do not guarantee a third, and we make no claim beyond $n = 4$.
item.dc:creator: Remus Osan

item.title: Fuglede--Kadison Determinants of Shifted Matrix Semicircles
item.description: arXiv:2610.15180v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove a variational formula for the Fuglede-Kadison determinant of a self-adjoint matrix semicircle $S_a = a \otimes 1 + \sum_j A_j \otimes s_j$ with deterministic mean $a$. For every real $z$, $\log \Delta(S_a - z) = -1/2 + \inf_b F_z(b)$, where the infimum is over positive definite matrices $b$ such that the map $X \mapsto bXb - \sum_j A_j X A_j$ is positive semidefinite, and $F_z$ is an explicit geodesically convex function. Both sides equal $-\infty$ exactly when $z$ is an atom of the spectral measure. The formula was proposed, without proof, in a recent post of Speicher. In the centered case $a=0$ it gives a new proof of the Mai-Speicher capacity formula, and by hermitization it yields a finite-dimensional variational formula for the logarithmic potential of the Brown measure of an arbitrary matrix-valued semicircular element. The proof identifies the determinant with the value of the Dyson action at its critical point and rewrites this critical-point problem as a saddle problem in three matrix variables. For a spectral parameter $z + i\varepsilon$ in the upper half-plane, eliminating two of the variables gives a geodesically convex minimization whose global minimizer is the positive factor $b_\varepsilon$ in a symmetric unitary factorization of the matrix Cauchy transform. The formula on the real axis follows by letting $\varepsilon \to 0$ in the optimal values, with no compactness assumption on the minimizers. At points where the boundary value of the Cauchy transform is nondegenerate, the scales $b_\varepsilon$ converge and the infimum is attained at their limit; this minimizer lies on the boundary of the feasible set when $z$ is in the support of the spectral measure and in its interior when $z$ is in the resolvent set.
item.dc:creator: Vladislav Kargin

item.title: Optimal detection of geometry in random graphs and kernel matrices at critical thresholds
item.description: arXiv:2610.15272v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Detection of geometry in random graphs and matrices has been extensively studied in recent years. For testing a dense random geometric graph on $n$ vertices with latent points in dimension $d$ against an Erd\H{o}s--R\'enyi graph, the detection threshold $d\asymp n^3$ is well known since Bubeck, Ding, Eldan, and R\'acz (2016). We sharpen this result by establishing the optimal asymptotic testing error in the critical regime $d/n^3\to\lambda\in(0,\infty)$. The log-likelihood ratio is shown to be asymptotically normal and dominated by the signed triangle count. Moreover, we consider testing the rank statistics of inner products between latent points against uniformly random ranks. We show that ranks preserve all asymptotic testing information available in the full matrix models, and a cubic statistic based on rank statistics attains the optimal asymptotic error. This then yields an asymptotically optimal test for random kernel matrices with a possibly unknown, strictly monotone kernel. The proofs combine the classical framework of Davies (1985) and Le Cam and Yang (1988) for asymptotic normality under information loss with conditional limit theorems for the models in consideration.
item.dc:creator: Cheng Mao, Timothy L. H. Wee

item.title: Three Homoscedastic Gaussian Components Have at Most Four Modes
item.description: arXiv:2610.15369v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Gaussian mixtures can have more modes than components. For three Gaussian components with a common covariance, four modes are attainable, whereas the best general upper bound was eight. We prove that four is the exact maximum in every dimension $d \ge 2$, for arbitrary means and positive weights. We further show that the sharp bound drops to three when the whitened means are collinear or form a right or obtuse triangle. The result covers degenerate modes without genericity or separate finiteness assumptions. Our proof maps modes to local minima of a separable free-energy functional on the probability simplex, reduces the problem to counting scalar inverse-function branches, and controls competing branches through curvature and stationary-height comparisons.
item.dc:creator: Rintaro Okahara, Kei Kobayashi

item.title: FirstFit coloring process of random bipartite graphs and an online coloring lower bound in the random order model
item.description: arXiv:2610.15468v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: FirstFit colors each arriving vertex with the smallest positive integer absent from its previously colored neighborhood. We prove that this rule can require $n^{\Omega(1)}$ many colors on certain bipartite graph of $n$ vertices even when the vertices arrive in a uniformly random order. This refutes the conjecture of Bosek, Gutowski, Laso\'{n}, and Przyby\l{}o [BGLP24] that FirstFit uses a polylogarithmic expected number of colors on every bipartite graph in the random order model. We obtain the lower bound by analyzing the FirstFit coloring process on random bipartite graphs, where vertices arrive to either side with equal probability, and with an independent edge density $n^{-x}$ for some $0 < x < 1$. Our result can also be viewed as a qualitative strengthening of Ku\v{c}era [Ku\v{c}91], who showed that, for every $\epsilon > 0$, there are graphs with chromatic number at most $n^{\epsilon}$ on which FirstFit uses $\Omega(n/\log n)$ colors in expectation under a uniformly random order. Our result shows that such poor behavior of FirstFit already occurs for $\chi(G) = 2$.
item.dc:creator: Yaqiao Li, Xin Li

item.title: Notes on Uniform Policy Score Bounds and Lipschitz Continuity for Truncated Gaussian, Product Cauchy, Boltzmann, and Softmax Policies
item.description: arXiv:2610.15690v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We establish uniform score bounds and Lipschitz continuity for truncated Gaussian, Cauchy, Boltzmann, and softmax policies under explicitly stated parameterizations.
item.dc:creator: Yanjie Dong

item.title: Robust Nonparametric Methods for $\alpha$-Mixing Sequences via Median-of-Means
item.description: arXiv:2610.15974v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The median-of-means (MoM) estimator is a robust alternative to the sample mean for heavy-tailed or contaminated data. While its non-asymptotic properties are well understood for i.i.d.\ samples, much less is known for dependent sequences. We establish non-asymptotic deviation bounds for the MoM estimator computed from consecutive blocks of an identically distributed $\alpha$-mixing sequence, both for a single mean and uniformly over a class of functions (the median-of-means process). All bounds remain valid, with explicitly adjusted constants, when a sufficiently small fraction of the blocks is adversarially corrupted. As applications, we obtain deviation bounds for a median-of-means Nadaraya--Watson regression estimator, for the MoM kernel density estimator, and for empirical and Bahadur-type estimators of Value-at-Risk and Conditional Value-at-Risk. Finally, we show that the sampling of bulk materials, where the measurements form a spatially dependent random field, reduces to the one-dimensional setting if the samples are taken in well-separated groups.
item.dc:creator: Attila Lovas, Marcell Tukora

item.title: Fourier entropy of threshold functions and their compositions
item.description: arXiv:2610.16069v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove the Fourier entropy--influence inequality for every linear threshold function, with a constant below $8.937$ and no restrictions on its weights or threshold. The argument applies to regular Boolean functions and gives logarithmic bounds for their Boolean combinations and for unions with bounded variable overlap. Character multiplication preserves the estimates and yields bounds by influence minus variance. Under arbitrary product measures, symmetric thresholds satisfy the strengthened inequality needed for read-once composition, uniformly in depth and fan-in. A joint description of each Fourier set refines the overlap estimate and recovers constant bounds for addressing. Exact selector identities extend the bound to orthogonal multiplexers with shared data. Rare activation preserves the optimal constant of unrestricted FEI. The proofs combine pivotal antichains, spectral reference measures, and product-measure composition.
item.dc:creator: Yitzchak Shmalo

item.title: Wasserstein rates of all orders for the Sato-Tate law of Kloosterman sums
item.description: arXiv:2610.16169v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $\mu_q$ be the distribution of the normalized Kloosterman sums $\mathrm{Kl}(a;q)$, $a\in\mathbb{F}_q^\times$, and let $\mu_{\mathrm{ST}}$ be the Sato--Tate law. We prove $W_s(\mu_q,\mu_{\mathrm{ST}})\ll q^{-1/3}$ for $1\le s\le2$, $W_s(\mu_q,\mu_{\mathrm{ST}})\ll q^{-1/6-1/(3s)}$ for $2\le s<\infty$, and $W_\infty(\mu_q,\mu_{\mathrm{ST}})\ll q^{-1/6}$, answering a question of Kowalski and Untrau. More generally, we bound $W_s(\mu,\mu_{\mathrm{ST}})$ for all $s$ whenever the Chebyshev moments of $\mu$ satisfy bounds of Katz type. For $s=2$ the bound also follows from a smoothing inequality of Borda and Cuenin; for $s>2$ and $s=\infty$ our bounds are stronger. The proof uses the quantile coupling, which arises from Stieltjes sums over two different intervals whose cells are paired so as to balance two measures, and which is optimal for all $s$ simultaneously; an explicit $W_2$ smoothing inequality relative to $\mu_{\mathrm{ST}}$; and a sharp comparison between $W_s$ and the Kolmogorov distance for laws with square-root edges. The last result shows that $q^{-1/6}$ is the best rate for $W_\infty$ obtainable from Niederreiter's discrepancy bound. Numerically, for primes $10^3<p<10^6$, all these distances appear to decay like $p^{-1/2}$.
item.dc:creator: Amir M. Rahimi

item.title: A Proof of the Erd\H{o}s Matching Conjecture for Large Matchings via Sharp Tail Probability for Sums of i.i.d. Nonnegative Random Variables
item.description: arXiv:2610.16203v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We resolve a conjecture of \L{}uczak, Mieczkowska and \v{S}ileikis on the maximal tail probability of sums of independent and identically distributed nonnegative random variables. Specifically, for every integer $k\ge1$ and every $0\le x\le1/k$, we prove \[ \sup_{\mathbb E X_1\le x}\mathbb{P}(X_1+\cdots+X_k\ge1) =\max\{1-(1-x)^k,(kx)^k\}, \] where the supremum is over nonnegative i.i.d.\ random variables $X_1,\ldots,X_k$. We also characterize all maximizing distributions. Using this result, we prove the Erd\H{o}s Matching Conjecture for every fixed $k\ge3$, all sufficiently large $s$, and every $n\ge k(s+1)$. More specifically, we show that in this range, the maximum number of edges in an $n$-vertex $k$-uniform hypergraph containing no $s+1$ pairwise disjoint edges is \[ \max\left\{ \binom{k(s+1)-1}{k}, \binom nk-\binom{n-s}{k} \right\}. \] Moreover, every extremal family consists either of all $k$-sets meeting a fixed $s$-set or of all $k$-sets contained in a fixed $(k(s+1)-1)$-set.
item.dc:creator: Cheng Chi, Shuang Sun, Yan Wang

item.title: Classical and Quantum Information Measures Characterizing Convertibility: An Axiomatic Approach
item.description: arXiv:2610.16267v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this PhD thesis, we take an axiomatic approach to studying multivariate divergences, which are measures of the information content of a tuple of classical or quantum states. These divergences are studied in the context of large-sample and catalytic convertibility of tuples of states. This type of convertibility is characterized by the ordering of an axiomatically defined family of divergences. In this thesis, we identify this family of divergences explicitly for two scenarios, one classical and one quantum. In the classical setting, we show that the relevant divergences are certain generalizations of the bivariate R\'enyi divergences. Unlike previous studies, we do not require the distributions to have the same support, yielding interesting new divergences. In the quantum setting, we consider pairs of classical-quantum states with pure component states, and find that majorization is characterized by all $\alpha$-$z$ relative entropies for $\alpha<1$. This demonstrates the first operational interpretation of these relative entropies.
item.dc:creator: Frits Verhagen

item.title: The relation between non-exchangeability and radial asymmetry of copulas
item.description: arXiv:2610.16631v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Non-exchangeability and radial asymmetry have got substantial attention in the literature, but relation between the two has not been studied yet. We propose the question: if a copula has a given degree of radial asymmetry, what is the range of possible values of the measure of non-exhangeability. We determine the set of all points whose first coordinate is the radial asymmetry of a copula and the second coordinate is its non-exchangeability. We show that this set is a non-convex hexagon.
item.dc:creator: Damjana Kokol Bukov\v{s}ek, Toma\v{z} Ko\v{s}ir, Bla\v{z} Moj\v{s}kerc, Matja\v{z} Omladi\v{c}

item.title: Averaged Annealed Markov Chains Achieve the Algorithmic Threshold for Tensor PCA, Part I: Glauber Dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2610.16705v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In the tensor principal components analysis (tensor PCA) problem, we are asked to recover an unknown vector in $\{\pm1\}^N$ from a noisy observation of its $k$-th tensor power, for a fixed $k\ge3$. Tensor PCA exhibits a well-studied information-computation gap: global algorithms such as spectral methods and sum-of-squares work above an algorithmic threshold, below which we know matching lower bounds (against these and some other restricted models of computation). In contrast, local algorithms such as Markov chains were only known to succeed from a random initialization at a polynomially larger signal-to-noise ratio, and were believed to be inferior to global algorithms for tensor PCA. We show that Glauber dynamics, when supplemented with annealing and ergodic averaging, achieves polynomial-time strong recovery above the algorithmic threshold from a uniformly random initialization, demonstrating that local Markov chains can succeed all the way down to the algorithmic threshold from an uninformative cold start.
item.dc:creator: Aniket Das, Tselil Schramm

item.title: GROMM: Generative Risk-neutral Option Market Models
item.description: arXiv:2610.16732v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present a statically and dynamically arbitrage-free European option market model with smooth interpolation between option prices, based on the SANOS framework, and prove that its dynamics admit a unique strong solution. In spirit, it is a stochastic model for local volatility when the latter is used as a representation of a European option price surface, not as a pricing model. We illustrate the strength of our approach on S&P Index Option data from January 2022 to August 2025. We show that the model's initial state fits within bid/ask for more than 95% of relevant market option prices. We then train the model dynamics under $\mathbb{P}$ and $\mathbb{Q}$ and show that the model is indeed free of arbitrage while fitting the dynamics of the market well. We also propose a range of BHW-tests to test for absence of arbitrage.
item.dc:creator: Magnus Wiese, Hans Buehler, Blanka Horvath

item.title: Very high genus double Hurwitz numbers via mixing times
item.description: arXiv:2610.16818v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We obtain very high genus asymptotics for double Hurwitz numbers when both the size $n$ and the genus $g$ go to infinity, under the constraint that $g$ grows much faster than $n$, more precisely that $\frac{2g}{n}-\ln n\to\infty$. Our proof relies on adapting arguments about the mixing time of the transposition random walk introduced by Diaconis and Shahshahani.
item.dc:creator: Baptiste Louf, Lucas Teyssier

item.title: Regularity theory for lattice based harmonic maps and low temperature Gibbs measures of the spin-$O(N)$ model
item.description: arXiv:2610.16833v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The purpose of this note is twofold. First, we revisit the classical regularity theory of harmonic maps in the setting of maps defined on a lattice $\mathbb{Z}^d$ instead of $\mathbb{R}^d$ or some other manifold. The target space of our harmonic maps will be spheres $\mathbb{S}^{N-1}, N\geq 2$. A harmonic map $\sigma : \mathbb{Z}^d \to \mathbb{S}^{N-1}$ is a map which in any finite subgraph $\Lambda$ minimizes the internal Dirichlet energy $\frac 1 2 \sum_{i \sim j \in \Lambda} \|\sigma_i -\sigma_j\|^2$ given the boundary condition $\sigma_{|\partial \Lambda}$. One key difference between our setting and the continuum is that our main H\"older regularity statement in a large domain $\Lambda\subset \mathbb{Z}^{d=2}$ does not require any regularity assumption on the map $\sigma$ restricted to the boundary of the domain. For example, when $d=2$ and $N=3$, the H\"older regularity induced in the bulk of the domain holds uniformly in all boundary configurations $\sigma \in (\mathbb{S}^{2})^{\partial \Lambda}$ (this is in contrast with the continuum which requires extensions in suitable Sobolev spaces). The fact we obtain results uniformly in the boundary conditions allows us to extend our results for positive temperatures. Namely, as $T \searrow 0$, we obtain a local regularity theory for all infinite volume Spin $O(N)$ Gibbs measures, at least when $d=2$ and $N\geq 3$. We also discuss implications of our analysis in dimensions $d\geq 3$.
item.dc:creator: Christophe Garban, Nathan de Montgolfier

item.title: Exponential profiles for the intrinsic volumes of Orlicz balls
item.description: arXiv:2610.16904v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: An Orlicz ball is the set of points where the sum of a fixed even convex function of the coordinates does not exceed a given radius, here proportional to the dimension. For a broad class of such functions, including non-homogeneous ones, we find the exponential rate of the intrinsic volumes whose order is proportional to the dimension and express it by a two-parameter variational formula involving only one-dimensional integrals. As a function of the order-to-dimension ratio, this rate is concave and continuous on the closed unit interval, and the convergence is uniform in the order. This proves the exponential-profile conjecture of Kabluchko, Marynych, and Prochno for these bodies and recovers their result for $\ell_p$ balls with $p>1$. The proof relies on the theory of large deviations. An exact formula for the Laplace transform of the intrinsic volumes in the radius, extending theirs for $\ell_p$ balls, plays the role of a moment generating function, and a Laplace method gives its exponential rate. An exponential change of measure, analogous to that used in Cram\'{e}r's theorem, then recovers the intrinsic volumes. The key step is a lower bound on the tilted density at its mean, obtained from log-concavity rather than a law of large numbers.
item.dc:creator: Mykyta Sadok

item.title: On the Stability of the Independence Number of the Distance Graph G(n,r,<s) for Growing r and s
item.description: arXiv:2610.16955v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We consider a random subgraph G_p(n,r,<s) of the complete distance graph G(n,r,<s) whose vertices are the r-element subsets of the set {1,...,n} and whose edges join pairs of subsets that intersect in fewer than s elements; each edge survives independently of the others with probability p. The stability of the Erdos-Ko-Rado theorem is the event that the independence number of the random subgraph equals that of the original graph, N = C_{n-s}^{r-s}. For fixed r and s, two-sided bounds for the critical probability, whose ratio depends on r and s, were obtained by P. A. Ogarok and A. M. Raigorodskii. In this paper we establish the order of the critical probability for growing r=r(n) and s=s(n): if min{C_r^s r^2, s r^3} = o(n), then the upper and lower bounds differ only by an absolute constant factor. The proof is elementary; only one of the two branches of the growth condition uses the complete nontrivial-intersection theorem of Ahlswede-Khachatrian.
item.dc:creator: Vsevolod A. Pokhachevskiy, Andrei Raigorodskii

item.title: Ideal Poisson--Voronoi tessellations for Finsler metrics on symmetric spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.17045v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Ideal Poisson--Voronoi tessellations are random tessellations that arise as limits of Voronoi diagrams for Poisson point processes as their intensity tends to zero. For the Riemannian metric on a symmetric space of higher rank, Fr\k{a}czyk, Mellick, and Wilkens (arXiv:2307.01194) proved that the corresponding ideal Poisson--Voronoi tessellation is almost surely completely connected, with an unbounded side between any two cells. This contrasts sharply with the geometry of ideal Poisson--Voronoi tessellations in hyperbolic spaces studied by D'Achille, Curien, Enriquez, Lyons, and \"Unel (arXiv:2303.16831). In this paper we introduce and study ideal Poisson--Voronoi tessellations for Finsler metrics on higher rank symmetric spaces. We show that ideal Poisson--Voronoi tessellations with respect to polyhedral Finsler metrics can exhibit either behavior seen in these previous works: generically they resemble the hyperbolic case, where almost surely all cells have bounded sides. We further introduce the ideal Selberg--Poisson--Voronoi tessellation of the space of positive definite symmetric matrices, which has particularly nice properties.
item.dc:creator: Colin Davalo, J. Maxwell Riestenberg, Anna Wienhard

item.title: On the foundations of logic and probability, II. Modal probability spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.17049v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A class of models which brings to the fore the inner logic of the calculus of probability instead of assigning probabilities to sentences is introduced and investigated.
item.dc:creator: Loic Cosyns

item.title: Sharp dimension threshold for unique FKPP steady states and BBM recurrence
item.description: arXiv:2610.17121v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We consider the existence and uniqueness of positive, bounded stationary solutions of the Fisher-KPP equation with Dirichlet boundary conditions. We establish that stationary solutions are unique, and exist if and only if the generalised principal eigenvalue is strictly positive (supercriticality), in dimension at most $6$. This is sharp: we exhibit examples both of non-uniqueness and of existence at criticality in dimension $7$ or higher, including for the classical reaction $f(u)=u-u^2$. This proves a conjecture of Berestycki and Graham in the affirmative for dimension at most $6$, and in the negative for dimension at least $7$. We thereby show that branching Brownian motion cannot survive globally without surviving locally in dimension $6$ or lower, but can do so in dimension $7$ or higher, mirroring the classical transition of Brownian motion from recurrence to transience from dimension $2$ to $3$. We further show that relaxing the strong-KPP condition results in a more general sharp dimension threshold for the uniqueness/non-existence result. These results are valid without any regularity assumptions on the domain boundary. As a corollary, we show that solutions of the evolution reaction-diffusion equation are always convergent in the long run in dimension at most $6$, whilst we exhibit non-convergent solutions in dimension larger than $6$.
item.dc:creator: Luca Rossi, Oliver Tough

item.title: H\"older regularity of the top Lyapunov exponent for random matrix products with low-dimensional equator
item.description: arXiv:2610.17153v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We investigate the regularity of Lyapunov exponents for products of random invertible matrices of arbitrary dimension $d\ge 2$. We prove that the top Lyapunov exponent is pointwise H\"older continuous with respect to the Wasserstein-Hausdorff distance in the space of probability measures with compact support, in the case where this exponent is simple and the equator has dimension equal to or less than one.
item.dc:creator: Ana Cristina Barreto, Adriana S\'anchez, El Hadji Yaya Tall, Marcelo Viana

item.title: Finite-order exponential mixing does not imply the central limit theorem
item.description: arXiv:2610.17162v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We show that finite-order exponential mixing does not imply the central limit theorem for smooth diffeomorphisms. For every integer $R\geq2$, we construct a $\mathcal{C}^{\infty}$ diffeomorphism $T:M\to M$ of a compact smooth manifold $M$ and a $T$-invariant probability measure $\mu$ such that $(T,\mu)$ is exponentially mixing of order $R$ for $\mathcal{C}^1(M)$ observables, but not of order $2R+2$. For some centred observable $f_0\in\mathcal{C}^{\infty}(M)$, no subsequence of the normalised sums $\frac{1}{\sqrt n}\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}f_0\circ T^i$ converges in distribution to a Gaussian law. In particular, exponential decay of two-point correlations implies neither exponential mixing of all orders nor the central limit theorem. We realise $(T,\mu)$ in two ways. In the first, $T$ is a fixed linear Anosov diffeomorphism of $\mathbb T^2$ and $\mu$ is singular with respect to Lebesgue measure. In the second, $M$ can be any compact smooth surface without boundary and $\mu$ is a physical measure whose statistical basin contains a nonempty open set. The main theorems have been formalised in Lean 4.
item.dc:creator: Bernat Bassols Cornudella, Matheus M Castro

item.title: Point Processes and Gap Statistics for Translation Surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.17277v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the behavior of saddle connection directions on translation surfaces from the point process viewpoint. We define a direction point process for saddle connections of length at most $R>0$ on every translation surface. Given a general ergodic $\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb R)$-invariant measure $\mu$ on a stratum of translation surfaces, we also define a slope point process associated with $\mu$. By utilizing the dynamics and geometry of strata, we show that for almost every translation surface, the direction point processes, rescaled by $R^2$, converge in distribution to the slope point process as $R\to\infty$. Using Palm distribution theory, we prove the existence of limiting joint gap distributions and obtain new regularity results for gap distributions associated with the general $\mu$. Finally, we study how these point processes and joint gap distributions behave as the genus $g$ tends to infinity. In the principal stratum, we show that the slope point processes, rescaled by $g^2$, converge in distribution to a Poisson point process. By passing to the corresponding Palm distributions, we show that the rescaled slope gaps converge jointly to independent exponential random variables, which is in stark contrast to the known non-exponential gap distributions in a fixed genus.
item.dc:creator: Kai Fu, Anthony Sanchez

item.title: Reach-Avoid Certificates for Contact-based Stochastic Hybrid Systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.17308v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This work studies certified reach-avoid control of stochastic hybrid systems in which a stochastic differential equation governs continuous flow and a controlled stochastic kernel governs guard-triggered resets. The input appears only in the reset kernel, where it determines the post-jump distribution. Certificates for such systems have so far assumed spontaneous or controller-chosen jump times, a finite horizon, or discrete-time dynamics; we certify, over the infinite horizon, that the target is reached before the unsafe set with at least a prescribed probability. First, we introduce reach-avoid contact certificates, whose flow and jump conditions are imposed only on a sublevel corridor, and prove that any such certificate with a compatible reset policy meets the specification; a pointwise safety filter extends this guarantee from verification to control by constraining arbitrary nominal controllers. Next, we prove that executions are non-Zeno and bound the expected settling time and reset count. We frame certificate search as a linear program over any twice-differentiable dictionary followed by independent verification. We illustrate our approach via comparisons where the certified region is a subset covering 93.6\% of the ground truth and where our certificate-based safety filter reaches the goal while reducing collisions from 68 to zero across 200 episodes of a dribbling ball problem.
item.dc:creator: Tianyi Xia, Ryan K. Cosner

item.title: DynaSPLIT: Strong tail-optimal scheduling for the M/G/n with heavy-tailed job sizes
item.description: arXiv:2610.17329v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the asymptotic response time tail in the M/G/n queue with heavy-tailed (regularly varying) job sizes. For this setting, strongly tail optimal policies are known only at lower load, where n-1 servers suffice for stability. At higher load, the tail optimal scheduling has been open. This paper presents DynaSPLIT, the first strongly tail optimal policy at high load. Together with prior work, this result shows that strong tail optimality is achievable across the entire stability region of the M/G/n with heavy-tailed job sizes.
item.dc:creator: Zhouzi Li, Mor Harchol-Balter, Alan Scheller-Wolf

item.title: Optimal Feature-Based Newsvendor Policies under Censored Demand
item.description: arXiv:2610.17465v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We investigate a newsvendor problem where a decision-maker observes a $z$-dimensional vector of covariates, and wants to learn how much stock to order given a sample of size $n$ of censored demand data to minimize costs. Demand is censored when insufficient stock is available to meet it, and past stocking quantities are known. We propose a new model-agnostic loss function approach to estimate optimal order quantities using observational data, and characterize the optimal newsvendor policy as the policy that minimizes our proposed loss function. Our method requires only a single estimation step, can be scaled to datasets with hundreds of thousands of data points, and does not suffer from the same instabilities as inverse censoring probability weighting methods. We describe how this loss function can be implemented in linear empirical risk minimization, kernel weights optimization and deep neural network algorithms, and provide excess risk generalization bounds for their out-of-sample performance. Moreover, we show through numerical experiments that our method quickly converges to the optimal policy on synthetic data, and leads to improved performance on real world retail data.
item.dc:creator: Joost van der Haar, Ilias Willems, Joachim Arts, Ingrid Van Keilegom

item.title: Alpern Lemma Independent of a Partition for Aperiodic Systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.17516v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that for every $(X,\mathcal{B},\mu,T)$, an aperiodic, probability preserving system and $\mathcal{P}$ a finite measurable partition of $X$, there exists an Alpern Multitower whose base is independent of $\mathcal{P}$. This removes the ergodicity assumption in the original proof of the independent Alpern Lemma of \cite{MR3373823}. As a consequence, we remove ergodicity assumption from recent results on limit theorems in deterministic systems \cite{Kosloff_Volny_2022,kosloffVolnyStableCLT,MR4955410}.
item.dc:creator: Nishant Chandgotia, Zemer Kosloff, Shrey Sanadhya

item.title: Optimal transportation under McKean-Vlasov dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2610.17626v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study a broad class of stochastic transport problems under controlled McKean-Vlasov dynamics, allowing control of both drift and volatility, with weak terminal constraints. In contrast to the classical Schr\"odinger problem, the reference dynamics depend on the evolving law of the process, leading to nonlinear optimization problems on path space, while the terminal constraint is formulated through weak optimal transport, permitting a flexible treatment of distributional targets. This framework encompasses several problems of current interest, including the mean field Schr\"odinger problem, martingale optimal transport, and Schr\"odinger-Bass bridges. We establish three main results. First, we prove the existence of optimal controls under general coercivity, continuity, and convexity assumptions. Second, we derive a convex dual representation that extends weak Kantorovich duality and stochastic optimal transport duality to controlled McKean-Vlasov dynamics. Finally, for the mean field Schr\"odinger problem, we prove convergence, at the level of value functions, of the associated finite-particle Schr\"odinger bridge problems to the mean field limit, thereby identifying the nonlinear problem as the exact infinite-particle limit of finite-particle Schr\"odinger bridges. As a byproduct, we establish the existence of an optimal mean field Schr\"odinger potential, providing a variational foundation for duality in nonlinear stochastic transport.
item.dc:creator: Camilo Hern\'andez, Ludovic Tangpi

item.title: Large deviation principle for determinantal point processes on Stein manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.17669v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper, we study natural determinantal point processes on Stein manifolds defined by canonical sections and plurisubharmonic weight functions. We present a natural condition on the weights under which these processes satisfy a large deviation principle with a good rate function given by the Fenchel--Legendre transform of the pluripotential equilibrium energy. Along the way, we prove some pluripotential theoretic results on Stein manifolds, such as the $C^{1,1}$ regularity of appropriate envelopes. These results are noncompact analogues of results of Berman and Berman--Boucksom on compact K\"ahler manifolds.
item.dc:creator: Kiyoon Eum

item.title: Distribution-Dependent Improvements of McDiarmid's Inequality via R\'enyi Divergence
item.description: arXiv:2610.17736v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We investigate whether R\'enyi divergence can sharpen McDiarmid's inequality and its distribution-dependent refinement induced by KL divergence. Starting from Marton's transportation proof, we show that its transport inequality fails in general when KL divergence is replaced by R\'enyi divergence of order $0<\alpha<1$. For sums of independent bounded random variables, however, the additivity of R\'enyi divergence allows us to adapt the argument and derive concentration bounds. For Bernoulli sums, these bounds strictly improve on the distribution-dependent bound induced by KL divergence over a range of deviation thresholds. We also establish a distribution-dependent refinement of Gilardoni's inequality relating total variation to R\'enyi divergence, providing explicit constants for our general concentration bounds.
item.dc:creator: Amedeo Roberto Esposito, Adrien Vandenbroucque, Michael Gastpar

item.title: $L^2$ convergence rates for singular stochastic wave dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2610.17815v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We establish quantitative hypocoercivity for singular stochastic damped wave equations arising in stochastic quantization. Building on the finite-dimensional argument of Cao, Lu, and Wang [Arch. Rat. Mech. Anal. 2023], we derive a dimension-free criterion that replaces uniform semiconvexity by a log-Sobolev inequality together with exponential lower-tail bounds for the bottom of the Hessian spectrum. We verify this criterion for the two-dimensional $\Phi^4_2$ and sine-Gordon models and for the three-dimensional $\Phi^4_3$ model, through estimates on the lowest eigenvalue of associated singular random Schr\"odinger operators. Combined with the continuum limit established in a companion paper, this yields exponential $L^2$ convergence to equilibrium for the $\Phi^4_2$ dynamics and for sine-Gordon with $\beta^2<2\pi$. For $\Phi^4_2$, we verify that in a weak-coupling, small-mass regime, optimizing the damping yields a kinetic relaxation rate of at least order $m$. This yields a genuine acceleration over the order-$m^2$ relaxation rate of the overdamped dynamics. The lattice estimates are uniform in the discretization for sine-Gordon throughout $\beta^2<4\pi$, and for $\Phi^4_3$ at fixed volume, including regimes beyond those for which the continuum dynamics is vpresently constructed.
item.dc:creator: Nikolay Barashkov, Giacomo Di Ges\`u, Petri Laarne

item.title: Optimal scaling and curvature correction for constrained MCMC on spheres
item.description: arXiv:2610.17946v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Sampling Gaussian measures restricted to nonlinear manifolds in high dimensions requires a proposal kernel that respects both geometric constraints and dimensional scaling requirements. We introduce tangent preconditioned Crank-Nicolson (pCN), which combines a manifold projection with a cancellation of the ambient Gaussian contribution, leaving only a geometric residual. Considering a shifted sphere with $\sqrt d$ scaling of radius and centre as a tractable benchmark embedded manifold, we prove that uncorrected tangent pCN results in a proposal noise scale of order $d^{-1/6}$ (compared to $d^{-1/2}$ for a tangent random-walk). We establish asymptotic optimal tuning for the geodesic expected squared jump distance which is maximised at an acceptance probability of 0.574 for the family of drift-corrected tangent proposals containing tangent pCN and tangent MALA. We also prove a joint diffusion limit for the parallel and orthogonal coordinates to the sphere's centre vector of tangent pCN. The orthogonal diffusion speed matches the limiting geodesic expected squared jump distance and is maximised at acceptance probability 0.574, whereas the parallel speed is maximised at 0.712, demonstrating that optimal tuning depends on the observable. We then identify an intrinsic precision correction characterised by potential Hessian and Ricci curvature that yields a proposal kernel with dimension-independent fixed step size limit. We discuss a generalisation to arbitrary hypersurfaces and present nondegenerate scaling of tangent pCN applied to conditioned diffusions under resolution refinement.
item.dc:creator: Nayef Shkeir, Tobias Grafke

item.title: Optimal Control of Mean-field FBSDEs and Classical Solutions of the Related Generalized HJB Equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.18015v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this article, we study optimal control problems driven by mean-field forward-backward stochastic differential equations (FBSDEs). The aim is two-fold: (i) to provide the unique optimal control; (ii) to establish classical solutions of the associated generalized Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman (HJB) equations on the space of probability measures. For (i), we study the coupled system arising from the maximum principle, which involves both the state FBSDEs and the adjoint FBSDEs. This system is non-standard and more complicated than that in standard mean-field type control (MFTC) problems. By extending the method of continuation in the coefficients to our framework, we establish the well-posedness result, and subsequently obtain the differentiability of the value functional with respect to the distribution argument --- thereby extending existing results for MFTC problems. For (ii), since the flow property does not generally hold for control problems of FBSDEs, standard dynamic-programming arguments cannot be applied directly. We therefore develop probabilistic approaches to the classical solvability of generalized HJB equations under three distinct sets of conditions. The auxiliary processes arising in these arguments differ significantly from those in standard MFTC problems. We establish new connections between the value function and the adjoint processes, derive equations for the relevant decoupling field, and obtain first- and second-order generalized HJB equations, including a coupled system on the space of probability measures. The standard HJB equations for MFTC problems are recovered as special cases. Our approach yields classical solutions without requiring non-degeneracy of the diffusion.
item.dc:creator: Ziyu Huang

item.title: Quantitative Convergence of Markov Equilibria for Time-Inconsistent Controlled Diffusions
item.description: arXiv:2610.18376v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Time-inconsistent stochastic control admits a natural game-theoretic interpretation in which successive decision dates are represented by different selves. In the Markovian framework of Bj\"ork-Khapko-Murgoci, the corresponding continuous-time equilibrium HJB system can be motivated by discrete subgame-perfect games, but the general discrete-to-continuous passage is not automatic. We establish a quantitative convergence theorem for a smooth uniformly elliptic class in which the control may enter both drift and diffusion. Using the exact sample-and-hold transition law on each time step, we construct, near a verified continuous equilibrium branch, a unique regular discrete Markov subgame-perfect equilibrium and prove first-order convergence of the continuation objects in an anisotropic $C^{2+\beta}$ topology and of the equilibrium policies in $C^0$. The key stability mechanism is structural: the discrete first-order condition forces the differential feedback correction in the frozen linearization to be nilpotent, which yields mesh-uniform block estimates through a two-norm dyadic Schauder argument despite the second-order coupling caused by controlled volatility. We also formulate a conditional transfer principle for structured polynomial-growth classes, with error-space stability stated as a separate hypothesis.
item.dc:creator: Sascha Desmettre

item.title: The Singularity Has a Distribution: Exact Timing Laws and Detection Limits for a Stochastic Intelligence Explosion
item.description: arXiv:2610.18445v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Automating AI research creates a positive feedback loop between software capability and research effort. We study a stochastic realisation of this loop in which independent, positive, multiplicative improvements arrive at a rate proportional to a power of current capability. Within this model, randomness leaves the deterministic explosion threshold unchanged but replaces the blow-up date by an explicit distribution. For equal-sized improvements the explosion time is a geometrically weighted sum of independent exponentials; its $q$-series representation gives its transforms, moments and tail behaviour, including a two-term small-time asymptotic. For Lomax-distributed improvement sizes the explosion time is exactly Gamma distributed. Self-similarity implies that, with parameters known, the relative uncertainty about the remaining time does not vanish as explosion approaches. We formulate a fixed-sample test between constant and geometrically increasing idea-arrival rates. If the baseline rate and the alternative log-rate increment $\ell$ are known, the minimum sample size at error level $\alpha$ is asymptotic to $(12z_\alpha^2)^{1/3}\ell^{-2/3}$, where $z_\alpha$ is the upper-$\alpha$ standard normal quantile. Uncertainty about the growth exponent near its critical value produces a $1/t$ tail with an explicit constant, and hence an infinite conditional mean waiting time, although explosion is certain given a positive exponent. Separate extensions show that a fixed deployment delay prevents explosion in the specified delayed-feedback models, that power-law diversion of effort shifts the growth threshold, and that in a deterministic oversight race a fixed allocation share does not change the asymptotic regime, except at a critical equality of exponents. Numerical illustrations, which are not empirical forecasts, show how timing and detectability depend on the granularity of improvements.
item.dc:creator: Xiaoyu Li, Zheng Gao, Chiwun Yang, Zhizhou Sha

item.title: A pedestrian's approach to Bayesian methods for inverse problems
item.description: arXiv:2610.18468v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In the past two decades, the Bayesian approach to inverse problems in infinite dimensional spaces has seen significant developments in theory, Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) methods, and in applications. The Bayesian approach in finite dimension produces posterior distributions of finite dimensional random variables. In infinite dimensions, the desired objects are random fields and their laws as measures on Hilbert or Banach spaces. There are many textbooks and tutorials available that explain Bayesian methods and MCMC in finite dimensions. To enter the field of Bayesian inverse problems in infinite dimensions, a newcomer has to engage with a quite diverse and extensive literature. The purpose of this article is to provide a basic path to the subject that is easily accessible to a reader with general knowledge in probability and mathematical analysis. We start with a swift introduction to the finite dimensional case. The infinite dimensional case is introduced for Gaussian priors on Hilbert spaces and Gaussian-type likelihood functions. In this situation, mere continuity of the forward map suffices to prove that the posterior measure is well-defined. We also give some new and simple stability results. Two application examples are elaborated, one finite dimensional, one infinite dimensional.
item.dc:creator: Heiko Gimperlein, Michael Oberguggenberger

item.title: Rapid Mixing of Stereographic MCMC for Heavy-Tailed Sampling
item.description: arXiv:2610.18513v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Sampling from high-dimensional, heavy-tailed distributions is a fundamental challenge in computational statistics, as many standard Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) methods mix poorly in such settings. Recently, Stereographic MCMC [Yang et al., 2024] and the Sub-Cauchy Projection Sampler [Grazzi et al., 2026] have been shown to perform successfully on such tasks. However, establishing their non-asymptotic convergence properties remains an important open problem. In this work, we fill this gap by establishing non-asymptotic upper bounds on the mixing time of the stereographic projection and sub-Cauchy projection samplers. Our results demonstrate that, under certain conditions on the target and initial distributions, the mixing time is polynomial in dimension for a broad class of distributions, including light- and heavy-tailed cases. Motivated by the theoretical analysis, we further establish a new weighted isoperimetric inequality that extends the classical version for log-concave distributions to the heavy-tailed setting with optimal dimension dependence. The proof techniques provide new insights into the geometric properties of heavy-tailed distributions that govern rapid mixing in high dimensions.
item.dc:creator: Federica Milinanni, Tyler Farghly, Jun Yang

item.title: Subgaussian Vector Balancing by an Ising Model
item.description: arXiv:2610.18639v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We show that the guaranties of the Gram-Schmidt Walk Algorithm of Bansal, Dadush, Garg, and Lovett can be achieved by an Ising model. Given vectors $v_1, \ldots, v_n$ of norm less than 1, we give a closed form for a centrally symmetric distribution on a vector $\sigma \in \{\pm 1 \}^n$ so that the signed sum $\sum_j \sigma(j) v_j$ is $1$-subgaussian. We show that the Glauber dynamics for this model mix rapidly provided that the norms of the input vectors are bounded below 1 by an inverse-polynomial. The proofs employ the theory of Lorentzian polynomials, and we use these techniques to show fast mixing bounds for other spin systems.
item.dc:creator: Heng Guo, Daniel A. Spielman, Xinyuan Zhang

item.title: Sampling with collective variables: Relative error analysis for umbrella sampling under general conditions
item.description: arXiv:2610.18717v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We consider the problem of estimating the expectation of a function (observable) with respect to a high-dimensional probability distribution, under the assumption that a low-dimensional collective variable map captures all the directions of slow mixing for the distribution. More precisely, under the assumption that the fibers of the collective variable map satisfy a log-Sobolev inequality, we establish non-asymptotic relative-error guarantees for this problem using the eigenvector method for umbrella sampling (EMUS). Our analysis applies to both log-Lipschitz observables and indicator of convex sets, and gives complexity bounds that are polynomial in regularity parameters and inverse relative accuracy, and exponential in the dimension of the collective variable space. As a relative error guarantee, our bounds apply to rare event estimation. We consider Gaussian biasing windows defined on a low-dimensional collective variable space and analyze a modified sparse matrix version of EMUS. The bounds quantify the effect of the map through mixing of the conditional distribution and fluctuation of the observable along the fibers.
item.dc:creator: Holden Lee, Matheau Santana-Gijzen, Jonathan Weare

item.title: A Rate Transfer Method: Convergence Rates in Stochastic Gradient Descent via Stochastic Calculus
item.description: arXiv:2610.18739v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We develop a rate-transfer method that converts finite-time Lyapunov estimates for an associated stochastic differential equation (SDE) into finite-time convergence bounds for stochastic gradient algorithms. Under generic moment and smoothness conditions, the convergence analysis of the stochastic gradient method reduces to a calculus argument verifying a Lyapunov generator inequality for the SDE. The method recovers established rates for classical stochastic gradient methods and provides a way to establish convergence rates for new optimization algorithms through calculus arguments applied to their associated SDEs.
item.dc:creator: Neil Walton

item.title: Functional calculus and martingale representation formula for integer-valued random measures
item.description: arXiv:1508.00048v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We develop a non-anticipative calculus for functionals of a continuous martingale and an integer-valued random measure. We first construct a non-anticipative functional derivative, which is shown to be the inverse of the stochastic integration for a dense functional class of integrands. We then show that this operator has a unique closure which is an isometry and defines a stochastic derivative acting on stochastic integrals. This stochastic derivative yields a constructive martingale representation formula and an orthogonal decomposition. The construction allows for random compensators, singular continuous time dependence and degenerate continuous covariation. On Wiener-Poisson space, the stochastic derivative is shown to be the predictable projection of the Malliavin derivative; we also obtain a factorization based on local mark gradients. We exhibit several applications of this framework to integer-valued random measures: sensitivity formulas and a convergent expansion for expectations under bounded predictable perturbations of the compensator, a change-of-measure formula for the derivative, a decomposition of the relative entropy in terms of the stochastic derivative, and a pathwise refinement of the Mecke formula.
item.dc:creator: Pierre M. Blacque-Florentin, Rama Cont

item.title: Commutative diagram of the Gross-Pitaevskii approximation
item.description: arXiv:1911.09635v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: It is well-known that the Gross-Pitaevskii variational formula describes the ground-state energy per particle of $N$-indistinguishable trapped particles (Bosons) in a dilute state in the large system size $N\to\infty$. The goal of the present article is to prove that the Gross--Pitaevskii formula also appears in the iterated limit of zero temperature and large system size of the product ground-state energy per particle of the $N$-particle Hamiltonian operator. For fixed particle number $N$, we moreover identify the low-temperature limit of the Brownian model with mutual intersection-local-time interaction as the ground-product-state energy per particle of the corresponding $N$-body system with repulsive Dirac interaction. This proves the conjectures of Adams, K\"onig and Bru from arXiv:math/0411660 and arXiv:math/0512305.
item.dc:creator: Stefan Adams, Chiranjib Mukherjee, Quirin Vogel

item.title: Free probability via entropic optimal transport
item.description:
arXiv:2309.12196v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $\mu$ and $
u$ be compactly supported probability measures on $\mathbb{R}$, and let $\mu  oxplus 
u$ denote their additive free convolution. We show that for all sufficiently large real $z$,  egin{equation} \int_{-\infty}^\infty \log(z - x) \, (\mu  oxplus 
u)(\mathrm{d}x) = \sup_{\Pi} \left\{ \mathbf{E}_\Pi[\log(z - (X+Y))] - H(\Pi \mid \mu \otimes 
u) ight\}, \end{equation} where the supremum is taken over all couplings $\Pi$ of $\mu$ and $
u$. Analogous formulas hold for multiplicative free convolution $\mu  oxtimes 
u$ and free compression $[\mu]_	au$. In this way, integrals of a log-potential against free convolutions can be expressed as entropic optimal transport problems. The corresponding optimal couplings admit explicit formulas, from which the standard $R$- and $S$-transform descriptions of additive and multiplicative free convolution are recovered. In particular, the optimizer $\Pi_z$ encodes the subordination equations via couplings of random variables. Our approach is based on a large deviation principle on the symmetric group, combined with the quadrature method of Marcus--Spielman--Srivastava.
item.dc:creator: Octavio Arizmendi, Samuel G. G. Johnston

item.title: Local properties for $1$-dimensional critical branching L\'{e}vy process
item.description: arXiv:2410.10066v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Consider a one dimensional critical branching L\'{e}vy process $((Z_t)_{t\geq 0}, \mathbb {P}_x)$. Assume that the offspring distribution either has finite second moment or belongs to the domain of attraction to some $\alpha$-stable distribution with $\alpha\in (1, 2)$, and that the underlying L\'{e}vy process $(\xi_t)_{t\geq 0}$ is non-lattice and has finite $2+\delta^*$ moment for some $\delta^*>0$. We first prove that $$t^{\frac{1}{\alpha-1}}\left(1- \mathbb{E}_{\sqrt{t}y}\left(\exp\left\{-\frac{1}{t^{\frac{1}{\alpha-1}-\frac{1}{2}}}\int h(x) Z_t(\mathrm{d}x) -\frac{1}{t^{\frac{1}{\alpha-1}}} \int g\left(\frac{x}{\sqrt{t}}\right)Z_t(\mathrm{d}x)\right\}\right)\right)$$ converges as $t\to\infty$ for any non-negative bounded Lipschtitz function $g$ and any non-negative directly Riemann integrable function $h$ of compact support. Then for any $y\in \mathbb{R}$ and bounded Borel set of positive Lebesgue measure with its boundary having zero Lebesgue measure, under a higher moment condition on $\xi$, we find the decay rate of the probability $\mathbb {P}_{\sqrt{t}y}(Z_t(A)>0)$. As an application, we prove some convergence results for $Z_t$ under the conditional law $\mathbb {P}_{\sqrt{t}y}(\cdot| Z_t(A)>0).$
item.dc:creator: Haojie Hou, Yan-Xia Ren, Renming Song

item.title: Robustness in the Poisson Boolean model with convex grains
item.description: arXiv:2410.13366v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the Poisson Boolean model where the grains are random convex bodies with a rotation-invariant distribution. A grain distribution is dense if the union of the grains covers the entire space and robust if the union of the grains has an unbounded connected component irrespective of the intensity of the underlying Poisson process. If the grains are balls of random radius, then density and robustness are equivalent, but in general this is not the case. We show that in any dimension $d\ge2$ there are grain distributions that are robust but not dense and give criteria for density, robustness and non-robustness of a grain distribution. For robustness, we provide a criterion that requires only information on the tail index of the marginal diameter distributions of the grains, as well as criteria that apply when diameters are sufficiently positively correlated. We also show the existence of grains, where the marginal distribution of the diameters does not provide sufficient information to determine whether the grain distribution is robust.
item.dc:creator: Peter Gracar, Marilyn Korfhage, Peter M\"orters

item.title: The circular law for random band matrices with arbitrary doubly stochastic variance profiles
item.description: arXiv:2410.16457v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the circular law for non-Hermitian random band matrices with independent entries and arbitrary doubly stochastic variance profiles. For matrices of size $n$ and bandwidth $n^\gamma$, we prove the circular law when $\gamma>\frac{5}{6}$ for Gaussian entries, or $\gamma>\frac{8}{9}$ for subgaussian entries under bounded-density assumptions. These thresholds improve the earlier sufficient conditions $\gamma>\frac{32}{33}$ for block band matrices and $\gamma>\frac{33}{34}$ for periodic band matrices. Subsequent work proves the circular law under the optimal condition of diverging bandwidth for specific open-boundary models \cite{han2025circular2} and periodic models \cite{han2026optimal}. Those results rely on local band structure and do not cover the arbitrary doubly stochastic variance profiles considered here. We also derive weak delocalization estimates for right eigenvectors in the Gaussian case. Our main technical input consists of polynomial lower bounds for certain intermediate small singular values, requiring no structural assumptions on the variance profile beyond double stochasticity. We also prove a circular law for the root empirical spectral measure of products of an arbitrary number of i.i.d. matrices, under bounded-density assumptions and a finite fourth moment. For smaller numbers of factors, we apply the same strategy as in our main band-matrix theorem to the cyclic linearization. For larger numbers of factors, the simpler structure of the product model allows us to apply the singular-value universality theorem of Hanin and Jiang \cite{hanin2025global} directly, together with a shifted log-determinant comparison. The two methods apply in overlapping ranges and together cover all growth rates of the number of factors.
item.dc:creator: Yi Han

item.title: Random $2$-SAT: The set of atoms of the limiting empirical marginal distribution
item.description: arXiv:2410.17749v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We show that the set of atoms of the limiting empirical marginal distribution in the random $2$-SAT model is $\mathbb Q \cap (0,1)$, for all clause-to-variable densities up to the satisfiability threshold. While for densities up to $1/2$, the measure is purely discrete, we additionally establish the existence of a nontrivial continuous part for any density in $(1/2, 1)$. Our proof is based on the construction of a random variable with the correct distribution as the the root marginal of a multi-type Galton-Watson tree, along with a subsequent analysis of the resulting almost sure recursion.
item.dc:creator: Noela M\"uller, Ralph Neininger, Haodong Zhu

item.title: Bregman variation of semimartingales
item.description: arXiv:2412.18345v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We define Bregman variation of semimartingales. We give its pathwise representation, It\^o-type isometry for martingales, and applications to harmonic analysis.
item.dc:creator: Krzysztof Bogdan, Dominik Kutek, Katarzyna Pietruska-Pa{\l}uba

item.title: Limit theorems for the number of sign and level-set clusters of the Gaussian free field
item.description: arXiv:2501.14707v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the limiting fluctuations of the number of sign and level-set clusters of the Gaussian free field on $\mathbb{Z}^d$, $d \ge 3$, that are contained in a large domain. In dimension $d \ge 4$ we prove that the fluctuations are Gaussian at all non-critical levels, while in dimension $d=3$ we show that fluctuations may be Gaussian or non-Gaussian depending on the level. We also show that the sign clusters experience a form of Berry cancellation in all dimensions, that is, the fluctuations of the sign cluster count are suppressed compared to generic levels. Our proof is based on controlling the Wiener-It\^{o} chaos expansion of the cluster count using percolation theoretic inputs; to our knowledge this is the first time that chaos expansion techniques have been applied to analyse a non-local functional of a strongly correlated Gaussian field.
item.dc:creator: Michael McAuley, Stephen Muirhead

item.title: The rank evolution of block bidiagonal matrices over finite fields
item.description: arXiv:2504.12275v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate uniform random block lower bidiagonal matrices over the finite field~$\mathbb{F}_q$, and prove that their corank undergoes a phase transition. First, we consider block lower bidiagonal matrices with $(k_n+1)\times k_n$ blocks where each block is of size $n\times n$. We prove that if $k_n\ll q^{n/2}$, then the corank of these matrices is $0$ with high probability, and if $k_n\gg q^{n/2}$, then the corank has Gaussian fluctuations. Second, we consider block lower bidiagonal matrices with $k_n\times k_n$ blocks where each block is of size $n\times n$. We prove that if $k_n\ll q^{n/2}$, then the corank exhibits the same constant order fluctuations as the corank of the matrix products considered by Nguyen and Van Peski, and if $k_n\gg q^{n/2}$, then the corank has Gaussian fluctuations. Finally, we also consider a truncated version of the first model, where we prove that at $k_n\approx q^{n/2}$, we have a phase transition between a Cohen-Lenstra and a Gaussian limiting behavior of the corank. We also show that there is a localization/delocalization phase transition for the vectors in the kernels of these matrices at the same critical point. In all three cases, we also provide a precise description of the behavior of the corank at criticality.
item.dc:creator: Andr\'as M\'esz\'aros

item.title: How fast does spectral radius of truncated circular unitary ensemble converge?
item.description: arXiv:2506.16967v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $z_1, \cdots, z_p$ be the eigenvalues of $A,$ which is the left-top $p\times p$ submatrix of an $n\times n$ Haar-invariant unitary matrix. Suppose there exist two constants $0<h_1<h_2<1$ such that $h_1<\frac pn<h_2.$ Then, $$\sup_{x\in \mathbb{R}}|\mathbb{P}(X_n\le x)-e^{-e^{-x}}|=\frac{(\log \log n)^{2}}{2e\log n}(1+o(1))$$ and further $$ W_{1}\left(\mathcal{L}(X_n),\Lambda\right)=\frac{(\log\log n)^2}{2\log n}(1+o(1))$$ for $n$ large enough. Here, $\Lambda$ is the Gumbel distribution and $\mathcal{L}(X_n)$ is the distribution of $X_n$ with $X_n$ being some rescaled version of $\max_{1\le i\le p}|z_i|,$ the spectral radius of $A.$
item.dc:creator: Yutao Ma, Xujia Meng

item.title: Scaling limit of boundary random walks: A martingale problem approach
item.description: arXiv:2507.10528v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We establish the scaling limit of a class of boundary random walks to the full spectrum of Brownian-type processes on the half-line. By solving the associated martingale problem and employing weak convergence techniques, we prove that under appropriate scaling, the process converges to the general Brownian motion in the $J_1$-Skorokhod topology. The main novelty of our approach lies in a result on the asymptotic behavior of the local time of the boundary random walks, allowing us to derive a CLT result for several Brownian-type limit processes on the half-line.
item.dc:creator: Juan Carlos Arroyave, Eldon Barros, Eduardo Pimenta

item.title: Conditional exponential directed last passage percolation under a one-point upper large deviation event
item.description: arXiv:2508.04954v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Under typical scaling, the last passage time field of the directed last passage percolation model with exponential site distributions converges to the KPZ fixed point. In this paper, we consider an atypical scenario in which the last passage time to a specific site is unusually large, and we explore how the last passage time field changes under this one-point upper large deviation event. We prove a conditional law of large numbers and compute the limiting fluctuations in certain regimes. Our proofs rely on an analysis of explicit multi-point distributions.
item.dc:creator: Jinho Baik, Dylan Cordaro, Tejaswi Tripathi

item.title: Translators asymptotic to vertical hyperplane
item.description: arXiv:2509.05650v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that a vertical hyperplane is the only complete translator, properly immersed in $\mathbb{R}^{n+1}$ ($n \ge 3$) and having finite topology, whose ends are $C^1$-asymptotic to vertical hyperplanes.
item.dc:creator: Yunfan Zhao

item.title: Denseness in total variation and the class of rational-infinitely divisible distributions
item.description: arXiv:2510.24219v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study a new class of so-called rational-infinitely (or quasi-infinitely) divisible probability laws on the real line. The characteristic functions of these distributions are ratios of the characteristic functions of classical infinitely divisible laws and they admit L\'evy--Khinchine type representations with ``signed spectral measures''. This class is rather wide and it has a lot of nice properties. For instance, this class is dense in the family of all (univariate) probability laws with respect to weak convergence. In this paper, we consider the questions concerning a denseness of this class with respect to convergence in total variation. The problem is considered separately for different types of probability laws taking into account the supports of the distributions. A series of ``positive'' and ``negative'' results are obtained.
item.dc:creator: Alexey Khartov
