item.title: On the $L^p$ Norms of Random Exponential Sums and the Metric Domination Principle over the Simple Random Walk
item.description: arXiv:2512.16124v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $R(n)$ denote the Simple Random Walk on $\mathbb{Z}$. We investigate the $L^p$-norms of random exponential sums of the form $S_A(a, y) = \sum_{j \in A} a_j e^{2\pi i y R(j)}$ evaluated on the torus $\mathbb{T}$, where $A$ is an arbitrary finite subset of $\mathbb{N}$. By establishing a strict inductive bound on the central binomial coefficient, we precisely estimate the collision probability kernel of the random walk. To address the non-monotonicity of the walk, we introduce a Metric Domination Principle, proving that the $L^2$-energy of the random sum over any sparse set $A$ is majorized by that of a contiguous initial segment of integers of the same cardinality. Interpolating between $L^\infty$ and $L^2$, we show that for any $p \ge 2$, the expectation of the supremal $L^p$-norm over all bounded coefficients is universally bounded by $C_p |A|^{p-1/2}$.
item.dc:creator: Yunfan Zhao

item.title: Random Polyhedral Cones I: Distributional Results via Gale Duality
item.description: arXiv:2602.08581v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $U_1,\ldots,U_n$ be independent random vectors uniformly distributed on the unit sphere $\mathbb S^{d-1}\subseteq\mathbb R^d$, where $n\ge d$, and consider the random polyhedral cone \[ \mathcal W_{n,d}:=\mathop{\mathrm{pos}} (U_1,\ldots,U_n) = \{\lambda_1 U_1+ \ldots + \lambda_n U_n: \lambda_1\geq 0, \ldots, \lambda_n \geq 0\}. \] We establish several distributional results for $\mathcal W_{n,d}$ and the associated spherical polytope $\mathcal W_{n,d}\cap\mathbb S^{d-1}$. Our main contributions include: (i) Let $\alpha_d$ denote the solid angle of $\mathcal W_{d,d}$ and write $m(d,k):=\mathbb E[\alpha_d^k]$ for its $k$-th moment. We prove the symmetry $m(d,k)=m(k,d)$. As an application, we compute $\mathop{\mathrm{Var}}[\alpha_d]=2^{-d}(d+1)^{-1}-4^{-d}$ and derive a closed formula for the third moment. (ii) For $n=d+1,d+2,d+3$ we determine the probability that $\mathcal W_{n,d}\cap\mathbb S^{d-1}$ is a spherical simplex, a spherical analogue of the classical Sylvester problem. In the case $n=d+2$ we also determine the distribution of the number of vertices of $\mathcal W_{d+2,d}\cap\mathbb S^{d-1}$. (iii) Let $f_\ell(\mathcal W_{n,d})$ denote the number of $\ell$-dimensional faces of $\mathcal W_{n,d}$. We prove a distributional limit theorem for $f_\ell(\mathcal W_{n,d})$ in the regime $n=d+k$ and $\ell=d-q$, where $k,q\in\mathbb N$ are fixed and $d\to\infty$. The limit law is a weighted sum of independent chi squared variables, with weights given by explicit eigenvalues of a convolution operator on the sphere. A unifying ingredient is an explicit coupling producing i.i.d. uniform vectors $U_1,\ldots,U_n\in\mathbb S^{d-1}$ together with i.i.d. uniform vectors $V_1,\ldots,V_n\in\mathbb S^{n-d-1}$ whose associated oriented matroids are Gale dual.
item.dc:creator: Zakhar Kabluchko

item.title: Generalized Mean-Reflected McKean--Vlasov BSDEs: Well-Posedness and a Markovian PDE Representation
item.description: arXiv:2604.14893v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper investigates a class of generalized mean-reflected McKean--Vlasov type backward stochastic differential equations (BSDEs). Our new framework combines a mean reflection constraint on the solution's expectation with a generalized integral with respect to a continuous non-decreasing process. We establish the existence and uniqueness of the solution. The uniqueness is derived via stability estimates, while the existence is proved by employing a penalization method combined with a smooth approximation of the obstacle. We further study a Markovian case, where the equation reduces to a nonlocal parabolic PDE with a mean constraint. We establish the well-posedness and the probabilistic representation of this problem, and we describe the regularity of the multiplier in terms of the regularity of the obstacle.
item.dc:creator: Ruisen Qian

item.title: Probability of Quota Violations in Divisor Apportionment Methods with Nonzero Allocations
item.description: arXiv:2605.06556v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Apportionment assigns indivisible items among groups. By the Balinski-Young theorem, no method can satisfy both house monotonicity and the quota rule. This paper investigates quota violations caused by nonzero allocation constraints, and derives exact probability formulas for their frequency. Such violations occur in systems like the U.S. House of Representatives, where each state is guaranteed at least one seat. We analyze the three-state case, introduce the $\tau$ statistic to parametrize population distributions, and prove an Asymptotic Quota Stabilization theorem: for fixed $\tau$, quota behavior stabilizes as populations grow, yielding probability results for quota violations determined by the set of ultimately violatory $\tau$ values. Applying this framework to the five classical divisor methods, we derive exact probability formulas. Additionally, we show that as the number of seats $M \to \infty$, these probabilities converge to method-specific constants. These results provide a precise, quantitative foundation for evaluating the fairness and frequency of quota violations in constrained apportionment systems.
item.dc:creator: Tyler C. Wunder, Joseph Cutrone

item.title: Signature Kernel and Schwinger-Dyson Kernel Equations as Two-Parameter Rough Differential Equations
item.description: arXiv:2605.08844v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We develop a rough-path framework for two-parameter rough differential equations on rectangular and simplicial domains, motivated by the signature kernel and Schwinger--Dyson kernel equations. The theory is formulated in spaces of jointly controlled rough paths and is based on a robust two-parameter rough integration framework. In particular, we introduce a notion of rough integration over two-dimensional simplices at low regularity extending previous results in the literature. Within this setting, we show that the signature kernel equation arises naturally as a two-parameter rough differential equation and establish well-posedness and stability. We also extend the Schwinger--Dyson kernel equation, previously formulated for bounded-variation paths, to rough driving signals, proving existence and uniqueness in appropriate controlled rough path spaces. In the smooth rough path regime, we relate the resulting equations to PDE and integro-differential formulations. Finally, we derive and analyse a numerical scheme for the rough Schwinger--Dyson equation, including runtime and memory complexity estimates, and illustrate its performance with numerical experiments.
item.dc:creator: Thomas Cass, Dan Crisan, Andrea Iannucci, William F. Turner

item.title: Properties of a Special Type of Filtration and its Martingale Criteria
item.description: arXiv:2606.04245v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This article investigates the structural properties of stochastic processes relative to a generalized single jump filtration, extending the framework introduced by A.A. Gushchin (2020) to the case of a non-trivial initial $\sigma$-algebra $\mathscr{H}$. By leveraging the general theory of processes and optional projection techniques, we establish fundamental measurability criteria for random variables and a complete characterization of stopping times and adapted processes. Furthermore, we derive comprehensive martingale and local martingale criteria, providing necessary and sufficient conditions for the preservation of the martingale property in this extended setting.
item.dc:creator: Assylliya K. Zhunussova (Lomonosov Moscow State University, Moscow, Russia)

item.title: Dimension-free Convergence Rate in Sliced Wasserstein Distance for Empirical Measures of Markov Processes
item.description: arXiv:2607.20150v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: To derive dimension-free convergence rates of empirical measures for Markov processes on a Banach space, we adopt the sliced Wasserstein distance (SW distance) induced by a probability measure with full support on the unit ball in the dual space. This distance refers to the convergence in finite dimensions, and is topologically equivalent to the classical Wasserstein distance when the Banach space is finite-dimensional. With the SW distance we derive dimension-free convergence rates for the empirical measures of ergodic Markov processes on Banach space, which can be sharp as illustrated by concrete examples. The study provides an efficient way to simulate infinite-dimensional distributions using sample trajectories of Markov processes, avoiding $``$the curse of dimensionality" in the classical Wasserstein distance. The main results apply to a broad class of infinite-dimensional models, and are illustrated by partially dissipative SPDEs in the end of the paper.
item.dc:creator: Feng-Yu Wang

item.title: Longest convex chains with i.i.d. points
item.description: arXiv:2608.09105v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Sample $n$ i.i.d. points from a triangle, according to some continuous density function. Given two vertices $A,B$ of the triangle, what is the maximum number of samples that form a convex chain with initial point $A$ and terminal point $B$? We show that to leading order, the answer is $cn^{1/3}$, generalizing a result of Ambrus and B\'ar\'any that considered uniformly distributed points. Furthermore, we express the constant $c$ using a variational formula whose maximizer (if unique) gives the limiting curve formed by the longest convex chain. By comparison, for $n$ i.i.d. samples from the unit square, the length of the longest monotone chain is asymptotically $c'n^{1/2}$. Despite the difference in scale, our formula is nicely connected to one established for $c'$ by Deuschel and Zeitouni.
item.dc:creator: Erik Bates, Arnab Sen

item.title: The variance of the Pitman--Yor process: Cifarelli--Regazzini-type identities and inversion formulas
item.description: arXiv:2608.10215v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The Cifarelli--Regazzini identity lies at the foundation of the theory of the Dirichlet process and has played a central role in Bayesian nonparametric statistics. By providing the generalized Cauchy--Stieltjes transform of linear functionals of the Dirichlet process, together with an analytic inversion, it yields explicit representations for the distribution function and density of the Dirichlet mean. This transform identity was subsequently extended to the Pitman--Yor process, a generalization of the Dirichlet process, leading to an analogous distributional theory for its linear functionals. Nonlinear functionals, by contrast, remain less understood, with results largely confined to a few examples for the Dirichlet process. In this paper, we move beyond linear functionals by considering the variance of the Pitman--Yor process, a genuinely quadratic functional. In particular, we establish a Cifarelli--Regazzini-type identity providing the generalized Cauchy--Stieltjes transform of the Pitman--Yor variance for general base probability measures under suitable integrability assumptions. We then analytically invert this transform under general conditions on the base probability measure, thus obtaining explicit representations for both the distribution function and density. Corresponding formulas are also obtained for the Dirichlet variance, yielding more explicit representations than those currently available in the literature. We also establish a distributional representation of the Pitman--Yor variance in terms of a Dirichlet process whose base probability measure is the joint distribution of the mean and variance of a suitably specified Pitman--Yor process, mirroring the classical within--between decomposition of variance and providing a quadratic counterpart to a known distributional identity for Pitman--Yor means.
item.dc:creator: Emanuele Dolera, Stefano Favaro

item.title: Correlated Gaussian Moments Determine Polynomials up to Orthogonal Equivalence
item.description: arXiv:2608.14475v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $P$ be a real polynomial of degree at most $m$ on $\mathbb{R}^d$. We construct finitely many correlated Gaussian moments that determine $P$ up to an orthogonal change of variables. The number of copies and the rational covariance matrices are specified in terms of $d,m$. On coefficient balls, the induced map on orthogonal orbits has a H\"older continuous inverse with an explicit exponent. For $m\geq3$, the normalised local stationary-phase expansion at the critical branch through the origin equals the Gaussian moment series. Its coefficients recover the same finite moment vector, without assumptions on the other critical points. If the leading homogeneous part has an isolated complex critical point, we compute the twisted de Rham ranks and construct formal lattices on each fixed coupling support.
item.dc:creator: Obayda Julien Assaad

item.title: Resolvent intertwining and spectral duality in Markov chains with geometric resetting
item.description: arXiv:2608.15140v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We uncover the resolvent origin of the spectral duality governing reset-neutral distributions in Markov chains with geometric resetting. Starting from the abstract conditions of Paper~III, we show that the spectral duality $B_\nu(z)=\kappa(z)\,A_\nu(\sigma(z))$ is equivalent to a single symmetry of the resolvent $R(\gamma)=(I-(1-\gamma)P)^{-1}$: the intertwining relation $[\Delta^2\mathcal{R},R(\gamma)]=0$, where $\mathcal{R}$ is the reflection operator of an involution $\sigma$ and $\Delta=\operatorname{diag}(\sqrt{\kappa(z)})$; equivalently, $\widetilde{\mathcal{T}}=K^{-1/2}\Delta^2\mathcal{R}$ is an involution. This symmetry determines the universal critical value $C^*=1/(1+\sqrt{K})$, with $K=\kappa(z)\kappa(\sigma(z))$, which depends only on the scalar $K$ --- not on the resetting rate $\gamma$, the reset distribution, or the particular chain. We characterize the class of $(\sigma,\kappa)$-reversible chains, encompassing both the biased random walk and genuinely non-homogeneous dynamics sharing the same $C^*$; a Doob $h$-transform realizes the duality $K\mapsto1/K$, hence $C^*\mapsto1-C^*$, with fixed point $C^*=1/2$. The orientation field admits the explicit resolvent representation $\psi(\gamma)=R(\gamma)(b^{(0)}-C^*b)$: its gauge-normalized form $\Delta^{-1}\psi(\gamma)$ is antisymmetric under $\sigma$, it has an exact node at the fixed point of $\sigma$, and it governs the exact sign law $\operatorname{sgn}(C(\pi,\gamma)-C^*) =\operatorname{sgn}\langle\pi,\psi(\gamma)\rangle$. Numerical experiments confirm the theory to machine precision. These results establish the operator-theoretic foundation of the spectral duality of Paper~III and provide the bridge to the information-geometric framework of Paper~V.
item.dc:creator: Juan Antonio Vega Coso

item.title: Solution to a fully coupled McKean-Vlasov forward-backward stochastic difference equation and applications to optimal control with law-delay
item.description: arXiv:2608.26424v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, motivated by discrete-time McKean-Vlasov optimal control problems with law-delay, a class of forward-backward stochastic difference equations is investigated. The main difficulties come from the absence of Ito's formula in the discrete-time setting, as well as the fully coupled structure in which the coefficients depend on both law-delayed and law-anticipated terms. Under suitable monotonicity conditions, the existence and uniqueness of solutions are established. Furthermore, a new monotonicity condition is introduced to address the associated optimal control problem. As an application, the unique optimal control for linear quadratic systems with law-delay is derived.
item.dc:creator: Duocheng Wang

item.title: Replica symmetry breaking at arbitrary depth
item.description: arXiv:2609.05317v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study finite-step replica symmetry breaking (RSB) in mixed $p$-spin Ising spin glasses at positive temperature and zero external field. For every integer $k\geq1$, we construct polynomial mixtures whose Parisi measures are exactly $k$-RSB, with each such phase persisting on an open set of coefficients. More generally, for a broad class of polynomial covariances with an $r$-RSB Parisi measure, adding the interaction term $\lambda q^p$ for sufficiently large even $p$ produces a unique $r$-RSB-to-$(r+1)$-RSB transition as $\lambda$ varies near a critical value. Since such covariances exist for every $r\geq0$, this yields transitions of arbitrary depth. The main idea of the proof is that, for large $p$, the perturbation $\lambda q^p$ is negligible for overlaps bounded away from $1$, while its effect is concentrated at overlaps very close to $1$.
item.dc:creator: P. M. Aronow, Patrick Lopatto

item.title: Exact Asymptotics for the 2D Euclidean Random Matching Problem
item.description: arXiv:2609.08717v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We determine the exact first-order asymptotics of the expected optimal cost in two-dimensional random bipartite matching, for every finite power cost $q \ge 1$, on the flat torus. In the endpoint case $q=1$, this answers a question by Talagrand, in the periodic case. The argument involves the closely related asymptotics of the energy of the solution of the $p$-Poisson equation with a regularized white-noise source. In the limit of vanishing regularization parameter, we identify this energy as the solution of a Variational Martingale Problem on a limiting Gaussian filtration, whose value is characterized by a parabolic Monge-Amp\`ere flow.
item.dc:creator: Victor Armegioiu, Michael Goldman, Francesco Grotto, Dario Trevisan

item.title: Gaussian Approximation in Wasserstein-p: Markovian Martingale Differences and Stochastic Approximation
item.description: arXiv:2609.09480v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We establish nonasymptotic Gaussian approximation bounds in higher-order Wasserstein distance $W_p$, $p\geq2$, for deterministic matrix-weighted sums of multivariate Poisson martingale differences generated by uniformly ergodic Markov chains. Under an $L^{(2+\eta)p}$-moment condition, $\eta>0$, we obtain the explicit bound $$O\left(p^3\|A\|_4^2+pd^{1/4}\|A\|_2^{1/2}\|A\|_4^2\right),$$ where $A\in\mathbb{R}^n$ collects the moment sizes of the weighted increments. When these sizes are of order $n^{-1/2}$, the bound achieves the first optimal $O(n^{-1/2})$ rate for fixed $p$ and $d$. Consequently, we also obtain the first optimal $O(n^{-1/2})$ $W_p$ Gaussian approximation rate for multivariate additive functionals of uniformly ergodic Markov chains. Our analysis develops two techniques for addressing the interplay between higher-order Wasserstein distance and temporal dependence. First, building on the Ornstein--Uhlenbeck relative-score approach of Fang and Koike (2023), we formulate the bound in terms of antisymmetric Stein couplings while retaining the conditional tensor structure. Second, we develop a refresh-then-maximal coupling that combines an independent first-step resampling, which preserves the desired Stein identity, with a subsequent maximal coupling that provides effective control of the coupling increment. We apply these bounds to nonlinear Markovian stochastic approximation by decomposing normalized errors into matrix-weighted Poisson martingale sums and remainders. This yields the first sharp $W_p$ Gaussian approximation rates for both last iterates and Polyak--Ruppert averages. In particular, the optimized rates are $O(n^{-1/3})$ for polynomial-stepsize last iterates and $O(n^{-1/4})$ for Polyak--Ruppert averages, with an $O(n^{-1/2})$ rate for harmonic-stepsize last iterates under an additional spectral condition.
item.dc:creator: Yixuan Zhang, Qiaomin Xie

item.title: Diffusion processes with $b\in L_{(p,q),\text{loc}}$
item.description: arXiv:2609.14847v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present some conditions in case $b\in L_{(p,q),\text{loc}}$ sufficient to guarantee the existence of a strong Markov diffusion process with drift $b$ and uniformly nondegenerate bounded matrix-valued diffusion. An example is given to illustrate how close these conditions are to be necessary.
item.dc:creator: N. V. Krylov

item.title: Sudakov Minoration for Unconditional Log-Concave Vectors
item.description: arXiv:2609.31782v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Sudakov minoration asks whether a large family of separated random linear forms must have a large expected maximum. We present a proof candidate for this principle for all unconditional log-concave vectors. The argument starts with a classical reduction to sparse coordinate supports. It then selects one feasible threshold witness for each label, removes a common coordinate core, and controls the remaining overlaps. The main analytic step is an exponential-moment estimate for a softened witness payoff. We obtain it by combining a one-dimensional clipping inequality with triangular transport, using log-concavity of the source and sign symmetry of the target. A Bernoulli comparison restores the signs at the end. The exposition includes historical context, a guide to the proof, all intermediate arguments, and explicit choices of constants. Two consequences concern covering numbers in the moment metric and concentration of bounded functions of the magnitudes.
item.dc:creator: Witold Bednorz, Rafal Martynek, Rafal Meller

item.title: Distances in $m$-ary recursive trees
item.description: arXiv:2609.33636v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce the $m$-ary recursive tree, a tree structure that starts with a single node. At each step of the growth process, a random node, called the recruiter, is selected, and $m$ new nodes are attached to this recruiter. The main objective is an asymptotic analysis of distances in this structure. We first derive the distribution of the depth of nodes in such a tree as a convolution of independent (though not identically distributed) Bernoulli random variables. This representation yields normal and Poisson approximations with quantified errors for the depth. We also investigate the height of these trees, that is, the longest root-to-leaf distance, via a coupling to a weighted random recursive tree with suitably chosen weights. The coupling transfers the results on a strong law and tightness from the weighted recursive tree to the $m$-ary recursive tree. Furthermore, we establish a bivariate limit law for the Wiener index, that is, the sum of all pairwise distances, and the internal path length, that is, the sum of the depths of all nodes, using the contraction method. As a novel technical feature of our approach, we employ weighted norms instead of Euclidean norms within the contraction method.
item.dc:creator: Kiran Bhutani, Ravi Kalpathy, Florian Lesny, Hosam Mahmoud, Ralph Neininger

item.title: Random $3$-regular graphs are not globally synchronizing
item.description: arXiv:2610.09135v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the homogeneous Kuramoto model on random 3-regular graphs. A connected graph $G$ is globally synchronizing if, for almost every initial condition, the gradient flow converges to a fully synchronized state, in which all phases coincide. It has been conjectured by Bandeira [Oberwolfach Rep. 21 (2024) 1163-1226] that a random 3-regular graph $G_{2n,3}$ is globally synchronizing with high probability. We disprove this conjecture in a strong way: $G_{2n,3}$ is not globally synchronizing with probability tending to 1.
item.dc:creator: Ciro Carvallo, Pablo Groisman, Dieter Mitsche

item.title: Optimal upper tail estimates for the edge eigenvalues of $\beta$-ensembles
item.description: arXiv:2610.11239v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Hermite and Laguerre $\beta$-ensembles are important and well studied models in random matrix theory, with the special cases $\beta=1,2,4$ corresponding to classical matrix ensembles. Although sharp moderate-deviation estimates have been established for the largest eigenvalues, substantially less is known for other edge eigenvalues. Even for the limiting distributions $TW_\beta^{(k)}$, the leading constants in the tail asymptotics are not known for general $\beta$ and $k\ge2$. In this paper, for each fixed $k\ge2$, we prove matching upper and lower moderate deviation bounds for the right tail of the $k$-th largest eigenvalue, with the optimal exponential constant $2\beta k/3$, for general $\beta$. We also establish sharp lower tail estimates for the second largest eigenvalue of the Gaussian and Laguerre orthogonal ensembles, with exponential constant $1/24$, same as for the largest eigenvalue. For $TW_\beta^{(k)}$, we obtain optimal upper and lower tail asymptotics for general $\beta$ and $k\geq 1$. We also obtain new stochastic domination results for the edge eigenvalues. Our proofs combine variational arguments from tridiagonal matrix models, last passage percolation, stochastic comparisons of sums of edge eigenvalues, and superposition-decimation identities.
item.dc:creator: Jnaneshwar Baslingker

item.title: Compatibility-based Bayesian inference: asymptotic limits, variational principles, and Wasserstein geometry
item.description: arXiv:2105.01962v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Approximate Bayesian Computation (ABC) replaces intractable likelihood evaluations with comparisons between observed and simulated data. We develop a measure-theoretic formulation of discrepancy-based Bayesian inference in which compatibility is encoded through nonnegative weights. For vanishing thresholds, we establish convergence of the corresponding posterior distributions in total variation. In the large-sample regime, we identify conditions under which the posterior converges to the prior conditioned on an asymptotic compatibility region, showing that concentration need not occur at a fixed positive tolerance. We also derive persistence bounds under weaker assumptions and prove stability of the associated entropy-regularized variational problems. For Wasserstein discrepancies, we obtain a geometric representation through distances from compatibility balls and an exact variational reduction to probability distributions over model laws.
item.dc:creator: Marco Tarsia, Antonietta Mira, Daniele Cassani

item.title: Optimal and Self Selection of Service Type in a Queueing System where Long Service Postpones the Need for the Next Service
item.description: arXiv:2208.09348v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study a make-to-order system with a finite set of customers. Production is stochastic with a nonlinear dependence between the ordered quantity and the production rate. Customers may have to queue until their turn arrives, and therefore their order decisions interact. Specifically, while being served, customers are aware of the queue length and choose one of two order quantities (or service types). The time to the next replenishment (their activity time) is stochastic and depends on the order quantities. A customer is inactive during service and while waiting in the queue. We refer to the type of service with a greater ratio of expected activity to service time as ``more efficient''. In the centralized case, the system is interested in maximizing the steady-state average number of active customers, which is referred to as the efficiency of the system. We show that choosing the more efficient service is not always optimal, but the optimal strategy can be approximated well by selecting one of three threshold strategies which depend on the number of inactive customers. In the decentralized case, each customer acts to maximize the fraction of time she is active. We observe that individuals and the manager have opposite incentives: When the queue is long, individuals tend to choose the long service, while the manager prefers the short service in this case. This makes the system difficult to regulate. However, we show that simply removing the less efficient service significantly increases efficiency.
item.dc:creator: Refael Hassin, Jiesen Wang

item.title: Balls in groups: volume, structure and growth
item.description: arXiv:2403.02485v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We develop a fine-scale structural theory for balls of polynomial volume in finitely generated groups. Our main result shows that a polynomial-volume hypothesis on a single ball implies that every larger ball can, after quotienting by a certain canonical finite normal subgroup, be embedded in a lattice of a Lie group whose connected component is nilpotent with sharply bounded index and dimension. These Lie groups and lattices form chains of successive quotients that are essentially unique, giving a quantitative fine-scale analogue of Losert's strengthening of the Mal'cev completion. This describes the fine structure of the group with sharp algebraic and quantitative precision; for example, it leads to sharp bounds in Breuillard, Green and Tao's finitary version of Gromov's polynomial-growth theorem. These results have a wide range of applications in various aspects of the theory of vertex-transitive graphs, including for instance random walks, percolation, and scaling limits. We obtain some of these applications in the present paper, and treat others in companion papers. Some are due to or joint with other authors.
item.dc:creator: Romain Tessera, Matthew Tointon

item.title: On the Regularity of Reaction Systems
item.description: arXiv:2409.05340v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Reaction networks have been widely used as generic models in diverse areas of applied sciences, such as biology, chemistry, ecology, epidemiology, and computer science. A reaction network incorporating noisy effects is modeled as a continuous time Markov chain (CTMC) and is called a stochastic reaction system. In contrast, the mean field limit of a sequence of volume-scaled stochastic reaction systems as the volume tends to infinity is modeled as an ordinary differential equation (ODE) and is called a deterministic reaction system. Non-explosivity of CTMCs and global existence of solutions of ODEs capture the regularity of respective dynamical processes. In this paper, we study the regularity of reaction systems, in both stochastic and deterministic senses. By constructing a simple linear Lyapunov function, we obtain the regularity in both senses for a class of reaction systems in terms of a simple checkable condition. In particular, we prove that (a) every binary mass-action system is regular, and (b) every second-order endotactic mass-action system is regular. We apply our results to diverse models in biochemistry, epidemiology, ecology, synthetic biology, and natural computing in the literature.
item.dc:creator: Chuang Xu

item.title: A unified spectral analysis of high-dimensional linear regression: debiasing and thresholding
item.description: arXiv:2502.17261v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We use spectral analysis to establish a unified theory of debiasing, thresholding, and simultaneous inference for high-dimensional linear regression with ill-conditioned designs. The methods include Ridge regression, spectral cut-off, and iterative and dynamical regression procedures. A common debiasing procedure uses two applications of the original linear algorithm with fixed parameters. Spectral analysis shows that debiasing squares the residual, while implementations based on matrix-vector products require no explicit spectral decomposition. Under explicit design, signal, and moment conditions, we establish maximum-norm consistency, recovery of the population threshold set, and error bounds for coefficient and noise-variance estimation. We derive Gaussian approximations for maximum coordinate errors and, under full column rank and deterministic sequences of regression parameters and thresholds, prove bootstrap validity for simultaneous confidence regions. Under additional regularity and gain conditions, we relate noise-free bias rates to best-worst-case error rates. Sparse and non-sparse regression experiments examine the effects of debiasing and thresholding under specified tuning rules. An elliptic inverse source problem extends the numerical assessment to reconstruction and empirical simultaneous coverage.
item.dc:creator: Ying-Ao Wang, Yunyi Zhang, Ye Zhang

item.title: Notes on Correlation Stress Tests
item.description: arXiv:2503.16200v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This note outlines an approach to stress testing of covariance of financial time series, in the context of financial risk management. It discusses how the geodesic distance between covariance matrices implies a notion of plausibility of covariance stress tests. In this approach, correlation stress tests span a submanifold of constant determinant of the Fisher--Rao manifold of covariance matrices. A parsimonious geometrically invariant definition of arbitrarily large correlation stress tests is proposed, and a few examples are discussed.
item.dc:creator: Piotr Chmielowski

item.title: Equilibrium Distribution for t-Distributed Stochastic Neighbor Embedding with Generalized Kernels
item.description: arXiv:2505.24311v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We extend the results by Auffinger and Fletcher in 2023 on the large-sample limit of t-SNE to a broader class of input and output kernels. We prove that under natural assumptions on the input distribution and the decay of the output kernel, if perplexity scales linearly with data size, the empirical measures and values of minimizers converge to an equilibrium distribution. We conclude with numerical examples comparing different kernels.
item.dc:creator: Yi Gu, Antonio Auffinger

item.title: Bivariate asymptotics via random walks: application to large genus maps
item.description: arXiv:2506.06924v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We obtain bivariate asymptotics for the number of (unicellular) combinatorial maps (a model of discrete surfaces) as both the size and the genus grow. This work is related to two research topics that have been very active recently: multivariate asymptotics and large genus geometry. Our method consists of studying a linear recurrence for these numbers, and can be applied to many other linear recurrences. In particular, we include a general theorem that yields asymptotics for such recurrences, provided that some assumptions are satisfied.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Elvey Price, Wenjie Fang, Baptiste Louf, Michael Wallner

item.title: Dirichlet $L$-functions on the critical line and multiplicative chaos
item.description: arXiv:2506.16115v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this article, we prove that the Dirichlet $L$-functions $L(1/2+ix,\chi_q)$, where $\chi_q$ is a uniformly random Dirichlet character modulo $q$ and $x\in \mathbb{R}$, converge as $q\to \infty$ to a random Schwartz distribution $\zeta_{\mathrm{rand}}$, which is related to complex Gaussian multiplicative chaos (GMC). This is the same limiting object that appeared in \cite{SaWe20a}, where the authors proved that the random shifts of the Riemann zeta function on the critical line $\zeta(1/2+ix+i\omega T)$, where $\omega\sim \mathrm{Unif} ([0,1])$, converge as $T\to \infty$. As an application of our method, we also prove that to the right of the critical line, that is, for $\Re(s)>1/2$, the convergence of the random $L$-functions $L(s,\chi_q)$ occurs in the space of analytic functions, if we exclude the zero probability (in the limit $q\to \infty$) event that $\chi_q$ is the principal character. This was already proven in \cite{Ba81a}, but our method provides a novel proof of this fact. Our results hold for moduli $q=q_n$ such that the smallest prime divisor of $q_n$ tends to $\infty$ as $n\to\infty$.
item.dc:creator: Sami Vihko

item.title: The p-spectrum of Random Wavelet Series
item.description: arXiv:2510.00622v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The goal of multifractal analysis is to characterize variations in local regularity of functions by computing the Hausdorff dimension of sets of points sharing the same regularity. While classical approaches rely on H\"older exponents and are restricted to locally bounded functions, $p$-exponents extend this framework to functions locally in $L^p$ and allow one to describe negative regularities. We establish a wavelet-based upper bound for the $p$-spectrum in terms of the asymptotic distribution of wavelet coefficients, extending the classical H\"older case. We then compute the exact $p$-spectrum of \textit{Random Wavelet Series} and show that, for non-negative regularities, this bound is sharp and is also attained by a prevalent set of functions with a prescribed wavelet statistic. Finally, we show that a different phenomenon occurs for negative regularities: contrary to the classical H\"older case, Random Wavelet Series do not in general realize the maximal $p$-spectrum compatible with a prescribed distribution of wavelet coefficients.
item.dc:creator: C\'eline Esser, Thelma Lambert, B\'eatrice Vedel

item.title: Partition functions of two-dimensional Coulomb gases with circular root- and jump-type singularities
item.description: arXiv:2510.00843v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper, we study the random polynomial $p_n(\rho):=\prod_{j=1}^n (|z_j|-\rho)$, where the points $\{z_j\}_{j=1}^n$ are the eigenvalue moduli of random normal matrices with a radially symmetric potential. We establish precise large $n$ asymptotic expansions for the moment generating function \[ \mathbb{E}\!\left[e^{\tfrac{u}{\pi}\mathrm{Im}\log p_n(\rho)}\, e^{a\,\mathrm{Re}\log p_n(\rho)}\right], \qquad u\in\mathbb{R}, \; a>-1, \] where $\rho>0$ lies in the bulk of the spectral droplet. The asymptotic expansion is expressed in terms of parabolic cylinder functions, which confirms a conjecture of Byun and Charlier. This also provides the first free energy expansion of two-dimensional Coulomb gases with general circular root- and jump-type singularities. While the $a=0$ case has already been widely studied in the literature due to its relation to counting statistics, we also obtain new results for this special case.
item.dc:creator: Kohei Noda

item.title: Sampling from multimodal distributions with warm starts: Non-asymptotic bounds for the Reweighted Annealed Leap-Point Sampler
item.description: arXiv:2512.17977v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Sampling from multimodal distributions is a central challenge in Bayesian inference and machine learning. In light of hardness results for sampling -- classical MCMC methods, even with tempering, can suffer from exponential mixing times -- a natural question is how to leverage additional information, such as a warm start point for each mode, to enable faster mixing across modes. To address this, we introduce Reweighted ALPS (Re-ALPS), a modified version of the Annealed Leap-Point Sampler (ALPS) that dispenses with the Gaussian approximation assumption. We prove the first polynomial-time bound that works in a general setting, under a natural assumption that each component contains significant mass relative to the others when tilted towards the corresponding warm start point. Similarly to ALPS, we define distributions tilted towards a mixture centered at the warm start points, and at the coldest level, use teleportation between warm start points to enable efficient mixing across modes. In contrast to ALPS, our method does not require Hessian information at the modes, but instead estimates component partition functions via Monte Carlo. This additional estimation step is crucial in allowing the algorithm to handle target distributions with more complex geometries besides approximate Gaussian. For the proof, we show convergence results for Markov processes when only part of the stationary distribution is well-mixing and estimation for partition functions for individual components of a mixture.
item.dc:creator: Holden Lee, Matheau Santana-Gijzen

item.title: The Fourier estimator of spot volatility: Unbounded coefficients and jumps in the price process
item.description: arXiv:2601.09074v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study a Fourier-based estimator of the spot volatility of a semimartingale, originally introduced by Malliavin and Mancino, and extend its asymptotic theory. First, we remove the uniformly bounded volatility assumption and establish almost sure convergence of the estimated Fourier coefficients under mild integrability conditions. We further derive explicit convergence rates that yield almost sure convergence of the reconstructed spot volatility via Fej\'er inversion. We then extend the analysis to processes with jumps. In this setting, we provide a precise decomposition of the Fourier coefficient estimation error into diffusion-diffusion, diffusion-jump, jump-diffusion, and jump-jump interaction terms, and obtain $L^p$-rates for each component. We show that the estimated coefficients converge almost surely to the sum of the true volatility coefficients and an explicit jump-induced term. Moreover, we prove that an appropriate rescaling of the trigonometric reconstruction yields almost sure pathwise recovery of the quadratic jump process.
item.dc:creator: L. J. Espinosa Gonz\'alez, Erick Trevi\~no Aguilar

item.title: Cluster size distributions of discrete random fields
item.description: arXiv:2601.14586v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study size distributions of finite excursion clusters of discrete random fields on the integer lattice $\mathbb Z^d$. For stationary fields, we assign a unique root to each finite cluster and derive an exact representation of the root Palm size law through joint exceedance and exterior nonexceedance probabilities for complete connected shapes. Root sampling gives each finite cluster equal weight and remains well defined even when infinite components are present. We also study the cluster size law conditional on a specified site being a local maximum above the threshold $u$, providing a local formulation for nonstationary fields. Under stationarity and almost sure cluster finiteness, an exact change of measure shows that peak sampling reweights the root law by the number of local maxima in each cluster. For stationary Gaussian fields satisfying suitable conditions, the total variation distance between these laws decreases exponentially in $u^2$. Guarded spatial Monte Carlo yields unbiased estimators of cluster intensities, estimates of sampling uncertainty from independent realizations, and a finite sample certificate for root truncation error. We further establish sufficient exponential cluster size tail bounds at a fixed threshold and exact logarithmic Gaussian decay rates at a fixed cluster size as $u\to \infty$. The latter rates are characterized by quadratic programs retaining the exterior constraints needed to identify complete components. Numerical illustrations compare direct probability evaluations with Monte Carlo estimates and assess sampling uncertainty and truncation error. The general representations and estimators apply to both Gaussian and non-Gaussian fields, providing a probabilistic foundation for quantifying spatial extent in discretely sampled data.
item.dc:creator: Dan Cheng, John Ginos

item.title: Rough Martingale Optimal Transport: Theory, Implementation, and Regulatory Applications for Non-Modelable Risk Factors
item.description: arXiv:2602.00097v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The Fundamental Review of the Trading Book (FRTB) poses a significant challenge for exotic derivatives pricing, particularly for non-modelable risk factors (NMRF) where sparse market data leads to infinite audit bounds under classical Martingale Optimal Transport (MOT). We propose a unified Rough Martingale Optimal Transport (RMOT) framework that regularizes the transport plan with a rough volatility prior, yielding finite, explicit, and asymptotically tight extrapolation bounds. We establish an identifiability theorem for rough volatility parameters under sparse data, proving that 50 strikes are sufficient to estimate the Hurst exponent within $\pm 0.05$. For the multi-asset case, we prove that the correlation matrix is locally identifiable from marginal option surfaces provided the Hurst exponents are distinct. Model calibration on SPY and QQQ options (2019--2024) confirms that the optimal martingale measure exhibits stretched exponential tail decay ($\sim\exp(-k^{1-H})$), consistent with rough volatility asymptotics, whereas classical MOT yields trivial bounds. We validate the framework on live SPX/NDX data and scale it to $N = 30$ assets using a block-sparse optimization algorithm. Empirical results show that RMOT provides approximately \$880M in capital relief per \$1B exotic book compared to classical methods, while maintaining conservative coverage confirmed by 100-seed cross-validation. This constitutes a pricing framework designed to align with FRTB principles for NMRFs with explicit error quantification.
item.dc:creator: Sri Sairam Gautam B., Isha

item.title: Simultaneous random polytope approximation characterizes the Euclidean ball
item.description: arXiv:2602.18547v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this work, we present a new geometric characterization of the Euclidean ball based on approximation by random polytopes. We investigate when a single boundary sampling density is asymptotically optimal for two random polytope approximation problems, and show that for a convex body in $\R^d$ with $C^2$ boundary and everywhere positive principal curvatures, one fixed density minimizes the leading expected errors for any two distinct intrinsic volume differences of inscribed random polytopes if and only if the body is a Euclidean ball. We show that an analogous characterization holds for the volume and mean width differences of circumscribed random polytopes, and that uniform sampling gives the converse statement in both models. We also determine the unique density minimizing the average of two normalized leading errors, and obtain an explicit positive gap for every nonball. The proofs combine classical random polytope asymptotics, H\"older's inequality, and a curvature rigidity argument based on the Hsiung--Minkowski identities and Newton--Maclaurin inequalities.

item.title: Intermittent Cauchy walks enable optimal 3D search across target shapes and sizes
item.description: arXiv:2603.10655v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Efficiently locating rare targets requires balancing the exploration of novel space with the exploitation of local vicinities. While this tradeoff is well-documented in simplified environments, its behavior in realistic three-dimensional environments remains unclear. Here we analyze intermittent L\'evy walks in three dimensions and show that search efficiency becomes strongly dependent on target geometry, with volume, surface area, and elongation governing performance across the L\'evy spectrum. Against this geometric complexity, the Cauchy walk ($\mu = 2$) emerges as a robust, near-optimal solution across a wide range of target geometries. Specifically, we prove that for convex targets of surface area $\Delta$ in a domain of volume $n$, the optimal expected detection time scales as $n/\Delta$, and that the Cauchy walk achieves this scaling up to polylogarithmic factors, while other L\'evy strategies are suboptimal in different geometric regimes. Our findings provide a theoretical framework for biological movement patterns, including marine predator foraging and immune surveillance, and inform the design of efficient search algorithms for engineered systems such as autonomous nanoscale explorers.
item.dc:creator: Matteo Stromieri, Emanuele Natale, Amos Korman

item.title: The equivalence of precompactness, zero maximal pattern entropy and bounded mean complexity for finite partitions
item.description: arXiv:2603.19772v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper, we investigate several types of low complexity of finite partitions, including precompactness, zero maximal pattern entropy, bounded mean complexity and mean equicontinuity. We first show that a collection of finite partitions in a standard probability space is precompact in the Rokhlin metric if and only if it has zero maximal pattern entropy if and only if the collection of the characteristic functions of atoms in those partitions is precompact in $L^2$ if and only if it has bounded mean complexity with respect to the Hamming distance. Next, we show that for a countably infinite discrete amenable group acting on a standard probability space, a finite partition has zero maximal pattern entropy if and only if each characteristic function of an atom in the partition is almost periodic if and only if it has bounded mean complexity with respect to some (and hence any) F{\o}lner sequence if and only if it is mean equicontinuous with respect to some (and hence any) tempered F{\o}lner sequence.
item.dc:creator: Jian Li, Tao Yu, Xianliang Zhong

item.title: SPLIT: SymPathy for Large jobs Improves Tail latency
item.description: arXiv:2605.13749v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the asymptotic response time tail in the M/G/n multi-server queue with heavy-tailed (regularly varying) job sizes, a setting representative of modern computing workloads. For single-server systems, tail optimization is well understood: under heavy-tailed job sizes, policies such as SRPT that strictly prioritize short jobs are strongly tail optimal, and giving any priority to large jobs is harmful. For multi-server systems, the question has been almost entirely open. This paper gives the first strongly tail-optimal scheduling policies for the M/G/n queue with heavy-tailed job sizes. Our central finding is that the multi-server case is intrinsically different from the single-server case: giving a small amount of ``sympathy'' to large jobs is essential for strong tail optimality. We establish strong (or arbitrarily close to strong) tail optimality across the full stability region, both with and without knowledge of job sizes.
item.dc:creator: Zhouzi Li, Mor Harchol-Balter, Alan Scheller-Wolf

item.title: $\alpha$-TCAV: A Unified Framework for Testing with Concept Activation Vectors
item.description: arXiv:2605.15688v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Concept Activation Vectors (CAV) and the Testing with CAVs (TCAV) method are fundamental tools for concept-based explainability in deep learning, yet their practical utility is limited by the variability across different samples of concept and non-concept examples. We analyze this stochastic nature of CAVs, and identify a fundamental flaw in the standard TCAV score, its instability by using a discontinuous indicator function. To address this, we introduce $\alpha$-TCAV, a parameterized unified framework that replaces the discontinuous indicator with a smooth function, which recovers TCAV as a limiting case. Under realistic assumptions, we characterize the score distributions and derive principled parameter choices: one matches the mean of its averaged counterpart, Multi-TCAV, with no larger variance using a single CAV; the other provides a calibrated probability that the concept positively influences the model output. Our analysis and experiments provide practical guidance and challenge the established practice of splitting the sampling budget across multiple CAVs.
item.dc:creator: Ekkehard Schnoor, Jawher Said, Malik Tiomoko, Wojciech Samek, Alexander Jung

item.title: The massless sine-Gordon model with logarithmic correlations in arbitrary dimension
item.description: arXiv:2606.06657v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this article, we study the sine-Gordon model with logarithmic correlations in arbitrary dimension $d \ge 1$. The model is defined as a Euclidean field theory whose interaction term in the classical action is \[ S_{\mathrm{int}}(\varphi) := 2z \int_{\Lambda} \cos(\sqrt{\beta}\,\varphi)\,\dx, \] where $\varphi$ is a logarithmically correlated Gaussian field on a compact domain $\Lambda \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ that coincides with the Gaussian free field when $d=2$, and where $z \in \mathbb{R}$ and $\beta>0$. We treat both the massive and massless cases, with the main emphasis on the massless regime. We construct the field without imposing boundary conditions, together with its charge and gradient correlation functions, and we show that the partition function is renormalizable. The results are non-perturbative, holding for all $z \in \mathbb{R}$. If $d=1$, our results are valid for the full subcritical range $\beta\in (0,4\pi)$ and if $d\geq 2$, the results are valid for $\beta\in (0,(d+1)2\pi)$. Our analysis is carried out directly in the continuum: we perform renormalization via a scale decomposition and control the partition function by controlling the renormalized potential that arises in this procedure, using the iterated Mayer expansion of Brydges and Kennedy~\cite{BrKe87a}.
item.dc:creator: Sami Vihko

item.title: An Operator-Theoretic Analysis of Nonlinear Filtering under Model Misspecification
item.description: arXiv:2607.11378v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study nonlinear filtering with misspecified initial distributions and dynamics, but a correctly specified observation model. Observations are treated as a random process generated by the true model, rather than as fixed realizations, and both the correct filter and the misspecified filter are analyzed under this common observation law. Our main result is a Bayesian total variation balance identity for the expected change in total variation distance under a Bayesian update: a covariance term minus a non-negative remainder. The identity characterizes conditional and averaged update non-expansivity. Combined with prediction contraction, it yields finite-time bounds separating the initialization error from accumulated dynamical discrepancies, while allowing expansive updates. When the averaged updates are non-expansive and a uniform joint prediction--update coefficient is less than one, a persistent dynamical misspecification yields an asymptotic error bound proportional to the one-step discrepancy. When the conditional updates are non-expansive, we characterize an accumulated joint contraction that implies almost-sure and \(L^1\) coalescence of the true and misspecified filters. Finally, we verify update non-expansivity for scalar Gaussian predictive laws under a variance-ordering condition and, separately, derive explicit prediction contraction bounds for truncated kernels and bounded transition functions with elliptically symmetric noise.
item.dc:creator: Fabi\'an Gonz\'alez, \"Omer Deniz Akyildiz, Dan Crisan, Joaqu\'in M\'iguez

item.title: On Mean-field Singular Stochastic Control Problems
item.description: arXiv:2607.26808v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study a class of mean-field control (MFC) problems with singular controls over a finite horizon, allowing for general dependence of the cost functional on the measure argument. We derive an auxiliary mean-field game (MFG) with singular controls, which we refer to as a potential MFG, and show that, under suitable convexity assumptions, any solution to this potential MFG yields a solution to the original MFC problem. We apply this general result to a version of the classical Monotone Follower Problem by I. Karatzas and S. E. Shreve (SIAM Journal on Control and Optimization 22(6), pp. 856-877, 1984) with scalar mean-field interaction. The associated potential MFG with singular controls is solved by exploiting its connection with optimal stopping for the optimization step and by a suitable application of the Kakutani-Fan-Glicksberg fixed-point theorem. In the case of strategic complementarities, the mean-field equilibrium (and hence the optimal policy of the original MFC problem) is characterized by a continuous nonincreasing free boundary that uniquely solves a nonlinear integral equation. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first paper to provide a complete characterization of the optimal policy in a finite-horizon mean-field singular stochastic control problem.
item.dc:creator: Andrea Amato, Federico Cannerozzi, Giorgio Ferrari

item.title: Nematic order in monomer-dimer models of Heilmann and Lieb with lateral attraction in dimensions $d\ge 2$
item.description: arXiv:2610.08600v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the $d$-dimensional generalization of Models II ($d=2$) and V ($d=3$) for liquid crystals introduced by Heilmann--Lieb (1979), which consists of dimers on the hypercubic lattice at chemical potential $\mu$, interacting via a hard-core repulsion and a lateral attraction between parallel dimers with coupling constant $b>0$. For $d\in\{2,3\}$, these models were conjectured to exhibit liquid-crystalline order at low temperatures provided that $\mu+2(d-1)b>0$. We establish nematic order for all $d\ge 2$ under the additional condition $(4d-6)b>\mu$, which corresponds to the physical regime in which misaligned dimers are rare on scales comparable to the correlation length of the one-dimensional reference system. While the treatment of orientational order here follows the approach of our recent work on Model I, the proof of the absence of translational order relies on a custom implementation of cluster swapping in the sense of Sheffield (2005). Consequently, we deduce uniqueness of Gibbs measure and anisotropic exponential decay of correlations within each oriented phase.
item.dc:creator: Qidong He

item.title: Maximal volume of convex bodies avoiding random points and lacunary dilates
item.description: arXiv:2610.09790v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: For a positive real lacunary sequence and any probability measure $\mu$ with polynomial Fourier decay, we determine, for $\mu$-almost every $x$, the asymptotic maximal volume of convex bodies avoiding the first $N$ dilates of $x$ modulo $\mathbb Z^d$. Among homothets of a fixed convex body, the maximal volume is asymptotic to $(\log N)/N$. When all convex bodies in the unit cube are allowed, it is asymptotic to $d(\log N)/N$. For independent uniform points in a fixed convex body $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^d$, the maximal volume of an empty convex body is asymptotic to $d\operatorname{vol}(\Omega)(\log N)/N$ almost surely. We also show, by constructing a one-dimensional counterexample, that lacunarity cannot be replaced by sparsity on sublacunary scales.
item.dc:creator: Yuval Peres, Bohan Yang

item.title: Sharp Minimax Gram-Determinant Asymptotics for Labelled Unit Decompositions of the Identity and Recent Developments on Makai's Conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2610.10979v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We show that Gonz\'alez Merino and Schymura's Conjecture 4.8, a sufficient condition for Makai's reverse isodiametric conjecture, fails in all sufficiently large dimensions. Its three-dimensional case follows from Aliev's proof. Pe{\l}czy\'nski and Szarek's construction for enclosing parallelepipeds implies this failure. Using random frames, we also determine the sharp exponential determinant guarantee for every fixed ratio greater than one between the number of vectors and the dimension.
